listings.name: Achilles Freedom Team of Wounded Veterans
listings.summary: Training and adaptive equipment such as hand-crank cycles so injured veterans can take part in road races up to the marathon, starting with beginner events like the 4-mile Hope and Possibility race.
listings.eligibility: All injured military personnel and veterans, combat or non-combat injuries.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact Achilles International (info@achillesinternational.org) or find a local chapter on its site.
listings.deadline: Rolling

capacity.served: 150,000 people served across Achilles programs; 68 chapters (undated); 8,000+ attended the 2026 Hope & Possibility 4M

listings.source_title: Achilles Freedom Team - Achilles International
listings.notes: Figures are organization-wide, not Freedom Team only.

listings.name: ACP Veteran Mentoring Program
listings.summary: Free, yearlong one-on-one career mentoring that pairs veterans and transitioning service members with professionals from more than 2,250 companies. A separate program serves active-duty spouses.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans and transitioning service members; active-duty military spouses through the Active-Duty Spouse Program. Applicants must meet ACP's program criteria.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through ACP's veteran application; spouses use the separate spouse application.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.served: 4,864 protégés completed mentorships in 2025; 44,000+ participants mentored since 2010

listings.source_title: Our Impact - American Corporate Partners
listings.notes: ACP reports 2,335 protégés got a job or promotion in 2025. Eligibility wording is from ACP's March 2025 news page; it links to program criteria (such as minimum active-duty time) that were not read.

listings.name: Maj. Gen. James Ursano Scholarship Program
listings.summary: Need-based grants for Army children working on a first undergraduate degree, renewable for up to four years of full-time study.
listings.eligibility: Unmarried dependent children under 24 of active-duty Soldiers, retired Soldiers, or Soldiers who died on active duty or in retirement. Children of Guard or Reserve Soldiers qualify only if the Soldier is on Title 10 orders for the whole academic year. Cumulative GPA of 2.0. FAFSA required.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the link in AER's yearly program guidelines; documents and the FAFSA are due by April 1. Reapply each year.
listings.deadline: 2026-2027 cycle ran Jan 1 to Apr 1, 2026; the 2027-2028 window is not yet posted
listings.source_title: Maj. Gen. James Ursano Scholarship Program for Dependent Children
listings.notes: Award amounts vary with budget, number of applicants and each student's Student Aid Index. AER publishes no counts on the page.

listings.name: General Henry H. Arnold Education Grant
listings.summary: Need-based grants for full-time undergraduate study for children and spouses of active-duty, retired or deceased Air Force and Space Force members. Amounts depend on FAFSA need and cost of attendance.
listings.eligibility: Children (who won't turn 24 during the award year) and spouses of Air Force or Space Force members on active duty, Title 10 or Title 32 full-time duty, retired, or deceased on active duty or in retirement; surviving spouses also qualify. Must be a full-time undergraduate at an accredited school with a 2.0 GPA and be the member's dependent for federal aid. Veterans and Guard/Reserve members themselves are not eligible.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online when the 2027-2028 application opens in early January 2027; a FAFSA is required. The same application screens for AFAS merit scholarships and interest-free supplemental loans.
listings.deadline: 2027-2028 application opens early January 2027; closing date not yet posted
listings.source_title: General Henry H. Arnold Education Grant | Hap Arnold Grant
listings.notes: AFAS publishes no counts of grants, applicants or dollars on the page.

listings.name: Emergency Financial Assistance
listings.summary: No-interest loans and grants for rent, utilities, medical or dental care, funerals, respite care, car repairs, travel emergencies and disasters, paid directly to the vendor.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty Air and Space Force members; Guard and Reserve on Title 10 extended active duty over 15 days; retired Air Force members (case-by-case, not ongoing); DEERS-enrolled dependents; surviving dependents.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the online application through the AFAS portal or at an Airman & Family Readiness Center. If you are not near one, request help from Army Emergency Relief, Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society, Coast Guard Mutual Assistance or the American Red Cross.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Online or at Airman & Family Readiness Centers
listings.source_title: Emergency Financial Assistance | Emergency Military Loans | AFAS
listings.notes: For Air Force and Space Force retirees, families and survivors, not all veterans. A January 2026 AFAS fact sheet describes a new single consolidated emergency application (not read in full).

listings.name: The American Legion Legacy Scholarship
listings.summary: Need-based scholarships for children of post-9/11 service members who died on active duty (up to $20,000) or of post-9/11 veterans rated 50% or more disabled (up to $5,000), for college, graduate school or trade school.
listings.eligibility: Children (biological, adopted, step or dependent) of post-9/11 service members who died on active duty, including federally activated Guard and Reserve; or children of post-9/11 veterans with a combined VA rating of 50% or higher. Must be a high school senior or graduate accepted to or attending an accredited U.S. school.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online starting January 1 through the Legion's application link. Include the DD 1300 or VA rating documents, FAFSA Submission Summary, financial aid award letter and itemized expenses; children of disabled veterans also need a DD 214 or NGB 22. Submissions can't be edited.
listings.deadline: 2027-2028 application opens Jan 1, 2027 and is due 11:59 p.m. Eastern, March 24, 2027; award emails May 10-24, 2027

capacity.served: 669 scholarships totaling $1,775,165 in 2026 (subject to final audit)

listings.source_title: The American Legion Legacy Scholarship | The American Legion
listings.notes: Also published: 2025, 559 scholarships ($1,778,165); since 2004, 2,559 scholarships ($11,445,857). Applicant counts are not published. Recipients may reapply up to six times.

listings.name: Temporary Financial Assistance (TFA)
listings.summary: A one-time grant of up to $2,500 to help a veteran's minor children with shelter, food, utilities and health costs during a family hardship.
listings.eligibility: Children under 18 (or under 21 if still in high school) who are the biological child, stepchild or legal ward of a current American Legion member veteran, or of a service member on Title 10 federal orders (no membership needed for active duty). Other available help must be used up first.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact your local American Legion post or department (state) headquarters; the application must start and be completed at the local level after a post or department review of need.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Through local American Legion posts nationwide
listings.source_title: About Temporary Financial Assistance | The American Legion
listings.notes: Veteran applicants must hold current Legion membership. Some older Legion pages say up to $1,500; the current page says up to $2,500.

listings.name: Service Dog and Guide Dog Programs
listings.summary: Free service dogs, PTSD service dogs, guide dogs, seizure response dogs, hearing dogs and MST service dogs, with two weeks of residential training in New York and lifetime aftercare; travel and lodging are covered.
listings.eligibility: Active military, honorably discharged veterans and first responders with a disability, PTSD, or vision or hearing loss. PTSD dogs: combat-related PTSD and at least 1 year in a mental health professional's care. Seizure dogs: at least one seizure a month. Guide dogs: legally or totally blind, age 16+. Must live in the U.S. or Canada.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete Part 1 of the application online; if you meet the criteria, Admissions sends Part 2 (medical and mental health reports, support person form and a video), followed by interviews and committee review. Responses within 15 business days.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.travel: Two-week residential training at the Smithtown, NY campus; training, placement, transportation and lodging are provided at no cost.
listings.cost: Free (owner pays about $75-$100 a month for the dog's ongoing care, as stated)

capacity.waitlist: Average wait for approved applicants is 9 to 12 months

listings.source_title: Program Admission - America's VetDogs
listings.notes: Hearing dog program takes a limited number of applicants; MST service dog program is a limited pilot. No total placement figures are published on the pages read.

listings.name: Dr. Aurelio M. Caccomo Memorial Scholarship
listings.summary: Two $12,000 scholarships each year for veterans and Guard or Reserve members with financial need.
listings.eligibility: U.S. citizen who is a veteran or a current National Guard or Reserve member, with a high school diploma or GED, enrolled or accepted in an eligible program, with financial need, not in default on a federal student loan, and with no drug sale or possession conviction.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Apply Here' link on the AMVETS page. Send your discharge papers (or commander's letter), transcripts, signed IRS 1040, FAFSA, acceptance letter, proof of expenses and a resume.
listings.deadline: Not published on the page
listings.source_title: Caccomo | AMVETS National Site

listings.name: AMVETS National Scholarships
listings.summary: $4,000 scholarships in three groups: veterans and service members, spouses and widows, and children and grandchildren. They fill the gap left after federal and state aid.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and active-duty, Guard or Reserve members; spouses and widows of veterans or service members; children and grandchildren of veterans or service members. Each group has its own application.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the 'Apply Here' link for your group on the AMVETS scholarships page.
listings.deadline: Not published on the scholarships page
listings.source_title: Scholarships | AMVETS National Site
listings.notes: AMVETS says the awards are given annually but publishes no number of awards or deadline on the page. Its separate WD-40 construction-trades scholarship (up to $5,000) last ran Aug 1 to Oct 15, 2024 and shows no newer window, so it is not listed.

listings.name: Army Emergency Relief Assistance Programs
listings.summary: Zero-interest loans and grants for emergency travel, rent and deposits, food, utilities, vehicle costs, medical co-pays, funerals, home repair and more, plus survivor grants and scholarships.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty Soldiers and dependents; Soldiers retired for longevity, medical reasons or at age 60 (Reserve component) and their dependents; Guard and Reserve on Title 10 orders over 30 days; surviving spouses who have not remarried; children of Soldiers who died on active duty or in retirement.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the online assistance application from a computer or phone, or visit the nearest AER office; if none is within 50 miles, apply online.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Online or at AER offices on Army installations

capacity.served: Over $13 million in educational scholarships provided each year
capacity.waitlist: Assistance is always provided within 48 hours (as stated)
capacity.figure_date: Annual figure as stated on the page read 2026-11-27

listings.source_title: Assistance Programs - Army Emergency Relief
listings.notes: For Army retirees, families and survivors, not all veterans. The page's copyright line reads 2019, so figures may be older.

listings.name: Army Women's Foundation Legacy Scholarships
listings.summary: Scholarships for certificate, community college, undergraduate and graduate study for women who served in the Army and their children, grandchildren and great-grandchildren, plus named awards for healthcare, nursing and disabled women veterans.
listings.eligibility: A woman who served or is serving honorably in the Army, Army Reserve or Army National Guard, or her lineal descendant. GPA 2.5 for certificate or community college; undergraduates need 30+ credit hours and a 3.0; graduate applicants need a 3.0. The PCSI award is for disabled women veterans rated 50% or higher, or their descendants.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the 2027 online application, then mail proof of service, transcripts, two recommendation letters and a typed essay to USAWF Scholarship Committee, P.O. Box 5030, Fort Lee, VA 23801. Apply for only one scholarship; AI-written essays are not allowed.
listings.deadline: All materials must be received by January 21, 2027
listings.source_title: General Information – Army Women's Foundation
listings.notes: The committee sets the number and amount of general awards each year. Named awards: M.M. Costello $3,000 (one), PCSI $5,000 (two), Six Triple Eight $2,500, LTC Nancy Porr $2,000.

listings.name: America the Beautiful Military Lifetime Pass
listings.organization: National Park Service / U.S. Department of the Interior
listings.summary: Free lifetime pass covering entrance and standard day-use fees at national parks, wildlife refuges, national forests and other federal recreation lands. Covers the holder and passengers in one private vehicle.
listings.eligibility: Any veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces, including National Guard and Reserves, and Gold Star Families (next of kin of a service member who died in a qualifying situation such as war or a military operation abroad).
listings.how_to_apply: Show a DD-2, DD-2765, Veteran Health ID Card, VA Veteran ID Card, or state ID/driver's license with veteran designation at a park entrance. A free digital pass is also available on Recreation.gov; Gold Star Families print a voucher from the NPS site.
listings.deadline: Rolling, available any time
listings.location: Federal recreation lands nationwide; digital pass online
listings.cost: Free (optional $7.50 shipping for a physical card via Recreation.gov; $10 processing via USGS Store by mail)
listings.source_title: Free Entrance to National Parks for Current Military, Veterans, and Gold Star Families
listings.notes: Does not cover camping, tours, reservation fees or concession-run activities.

listings.name: Warrior PATHH
listings.summary: A free 90-day, peer-delivered training program in posttraumatic growth that starts with a 5-day in-person initiation, followed by three months of support and accountability.
listings.eligibility: Combat veterans (anyone who deployed to or supported a combat zone) and active, reserve and Guard members, plus certified first responders involved in a critical incident. Must be active, retired or separated.
listings.how_to_apply: Check eligibility and complete the Warrior PATHH application on bouldercrest.org; a screening call with a PATHH Guide follows before dates are set.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Boulder Crest campuses (Bluemont, VA; Texas) and partner locations nationwide
listings.travel: Initiation is in person at a Boulder Crest or partner site. Travel coverage not published on the pages read.

capacity.served: 1,213 people trained in more than 156 programs in 2025 (Avalon Action Alliance total, which includes Warrior PATHH)

listings.source_title: Check Your Warrior PATHH Eligibility - Boulder Crest Foundation
listings.notes: 2025 figures cover the whole Avalon Action Alliance, not Warrior PATHH alone.

listings.name: Home Award and Home Modification Programs
listings.summary: Gifts mortgage-free homes to injured and disabled veterans and Gold Star families who do not own a home, and gives home modification grants to those who do.
listings.eligibility: Honorably discharged (or will be) injured or disabled veterans and Gold Star families. Home award: you and your spouse cannot own a home or land. Modifications: the veteran's name must be on the deed. New builds only in limited cases and only with VA SAH grant approval.
listings.how_to_apply: Review available homes on the website, then complete the online Home Award or Home Modification application with your DD-214, VA rating letter, photos, two letters of recommendation (one from a caseworker or veteran advocate) and signed waivers.
listings.deadline: Rolling; homes are posted as they become available
listings.location: Homes in various states as listed on the website; headquarters in Island Park, New York

capacity.applicants: The organization states there are far more applicants than available homes or modification opportunities (no count published)
capacity.waitlist: No specific timeframe for if, or when, an applicant may receive an award

listings.source_title: Home Program Details | Building Homes for Heroes Inc
listings.notes: Founded 2006; goal stated on site of reaching its 500th home by the end of 2026, but no current total is published. Modification grants are capped and may not cover the full cost.

listings.name: Service Dogs for Veterans (Veterans Initiative)
listings.summary: Free service dogs for veterans, including dogs trained to interrupt PTSD symptoms such as nightmares and anxiety, and dogs that retrieve items, open doors or alert to sounds; follow-up support is free.
listings.eligibility: U.S. Armed Forces veterans age 18+ with a DD-214; PTSD dogs require service-connected PTSD. Must be able to control and care for a dog.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit a Basic Service Dog Request online; staff review it (typically 4 to 6 weeks) and, if it fits, email a full application. The Veteran Program Manager can help with questions.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Regional training centers in Northern California, Southern California, Texas, Ohio, New York and Florida
listings.travel: Two-week Team Training class at a regional training center (the PTSD program is offered only at certain centers). Students pay their own transportation and meals during training.
listings.cost: Free (student pays own travel and meals during training)

capacity.waitlist: Not published; service dog candidates generally have the longest wait

listings.source_title: Veterans - Canine Companions
listings.notes: The veterans page says 'hundreds' of dogs have gone to veterans without an exact count; over 8,800 people with disabilities served overall. One of the six training centers is in Ohio, but the pages read do not say which centers run the PTSD program.

listings.name: Catch A Lift Wellness Program
listings.summary: Free fitness support for combat-injured veterans: gym memberships or home gym equipment, an 8-week one-on-one coaching program with veteran coaches, and an online wellness platform and peer community.
listings.eligibility: Veterans deployed to Iraq or Afghanistan (OIF, OEF, OND) with combat-related injuries and a VA rating of 50% or higher, at least 30% from one combat-related injury; must live in the continental U.S., Hawaii or Alaska.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply at catchaliftfund.org/apply with your DD214 (SSN blocked) showing Iraq/Afghanistan deployment and proof such as deployment papers, your VA rating narrative letter, and a photo. Or call 855-496-4838.
listings.deadline: Quarterly intake; the apply page showed applications closed because the quarter's spots were filled (its posted reopen date, May 5, 2025, is out of date)
listings.location: Online coaching plus local gym or home equipment nationwide

capacity.served: More than 14,900 lives lifted (cumulative, undated)

listings.source_title: Apply - Catch A Lift Fund
listings.notes: Spots fill each quarter; check the apply page for the current window. GWOT medals alone do not prove deployment.

listings.name: Children of Fallen Patriots Scholarships
listings.summary: College and trade-school support for children who lost a military parent in the line of duty or to a service-connected cause. Covers tuition, fees, books and supplies, plus a $2,150-per-semester living stipend, a $1,650 one-time computer stipend and a $500 pre-college stipend.
listings.eligibility: Children of service members who died in the line of duty or from a service-connected cause: high school juniors and seniors, students at an accredited college, trade or vocational program, or graduates with undergraduate student loans. Minimum 2.0 GPA for the previous term.
listings.how_to_apply: Enroll online at fallenpatriots.org, then email the DD1300 (or alternatives), VA certificate of eligibility, transcript, class schedule, itemized tuition statement and verification form. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks.
listings.deadline: Rolling; applications processed in the order received

capacity.served: Over 4,000 students in the scholar network; over $82 million provided since 2002 to over 4,000 children

listings.source_title: Children of Fallen Patriots Foundation
listings.notes: Details on stipends and documents are from the foundation's scholarship FAQ (fallenpatriots.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/CFPScholarshipFAQ7.pdf). The home page says the foundation is joining the Tunnel to Towers Foundation and current scholar families need not change anything. It also reports over 2,200 graduates supported.

listings.name: Coast Guard Mutual Assistance
listings.summary: Interest-free loans, grants, financial counseling and referrals for emergencies, day-to-day needs and education in the Coast Guard community.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty, Reserve and retired Coast Guard members, surviving spouses, civilian employees, Auxiliary members, chaplains and PHS officers serving the Coast Guard.
listings.how_to_apply: Start with a local CGMA Representative (use Find my Representative on the website) or call CGMA headquarters.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.served: Over $260 million disbursed to the Coast Guard community

listings.source_title: Coast Guard Mutual Assistance | Official Relief Society of the USCG
listings.notes: For Coast Guard retirees, families and survivors, not all veterans.

listings.name: Steven A. Cohen Military Family Clinics
listings.summary: Outpatient mental health care for veterans, service members and their families at 23 clinics and by telehealth, for PTSD, depression, anxiety, relationship and transition issues.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans including Guard and Reserve, regardless of discharge status, job or length of service; service members (active duty need a TRICARE referral); and family members of post-9/11 veterans and service members.
listings.how_to_apply: Request an appointment online or call the nearest clinic; telehealth is available where licensed.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: 23 clinics in 22 states and D.C., plus telehealth
listings.cost: Accepts most insurance including TRICARE; the network says cost is not a barrier (no fee schedule published)
listings.source_title: Homepage - Cohen Veterans Network
listings.notes: 'Cost is not a barrier' wording from a Headstrong resource page; Cohen's home page lists insurance only. No Ohio clinic confirmed from pages read.

listings.name: Disaster Relief Program
listings.summary: Emergency cash (paid by check) for food, clothing and shelter, plus supply kits with blankets and hygiene items, for disabled veterans hit by a natural disaster.
listings.eligibility: Ill, injured or wounded veterans or their spouse in the same household; surviving spouses receiving DIC or Death Compensation; surviving spouses of former POWs; surviving spouses of a disabled veteran killed in the disaster. Must be a disaster victim in immediate need. DAV membership and service-connected compensation are not required. One per family per disaster.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact your nearest DAV office through DAV's local office finder to inquire about disaster relief; DAV benefits advocates help with the request.
listings.deadline: After a disaster; no published deadline

capacity.served: Over $326,000 provided to 450 veterans across 21 states in 2025; 19,505 checks totaling $10,242,520 over the last 10 years
capacity.figure_date: 2025 (single year); 10-year total as stated on the page in 2026

listings.source_title: Emergency Disaster Relief for Veterans - DAV
listings.notes: The page gives the 2025 total as both $326,000 and $326,500. A March 2026 DAV news article says nearly $6 million in disaster relief over the past five years.

listings.name: DAV Patriot Boot Camp
listings.summary: Free three-day entrepreneurship cohorts with startup education, one-on-one mentoring, networking and a pitch contest for non-dilutive funding, for military-connected founders.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and military spouses who own or founded a scalable, growing for-profit business (franchises and nonprofits excluded). An EIN, website and recent revenue are preferred but not required.
listings.how_to_apply: Click 'Apply Now' for the current event on patriotbootcamp.org; seats are first come, first served. Join the mailing list to hear when applications open.
listings.deadline: Next cohort dates are not shown on the program page
listings.location: In-person cohorts in different cities; some programs virtual
listings.travel: DAV covers programming, meals and local transport for participants staying at partner hotels; participants pay their own travel to the city and their hotel

capacity.served: 1,346 alumni; 36 virtual and in-person programs held

listings.source_title: DAV Patriot Boot Camp entrepreneurship program for veterans
listings.notes: A DAV notice seen only in search lists the next cohort as Feb 17-19, 2027 at DAV headquarters in Erlanger, Ky., with applications closing Jan 18, 2027 or when full; not confirmed on the program page.

listings.name: DoD SkillBridge
listings.summary: Lets service members spend up to their last 180 days of service in civilian job training, apprenticeships or internships with approved employers while keeping military pay and benefits.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty service members (and select Guard and Reserve members under their service's rules) within 180 days of separation, with written approval from their first O-4 or higher commander. Finishing TAP is strongly recommended and may be required. Not for veterans who have already separated.
listings.how_to_apply: Find an approved opportunity in the SkillBridge search tool, work with your installation SkillBridge point of contact, and get the program application or MOU signed by you, your commander and the installation program manager.
listings.deadline: Rolling within the last 180 days of service; command approval required
listings.cost: Free; members usually pay their own travel to the program site

capacity.served: Over 22,500 service members enrolled in or completed SkillBridge in fiscal year 2022

listings.source_title: DoD SkillBridge Frequently Asked Questions
listings.notes: Figure is from GAO report GAO-24-107352 (Aug 2024), which also reports almost 12,000 participants in the first half of FY2024.

listings.name: Veterans' Priority of Service at American Job Centers
listings.summary: Veterans and eligible spouses get priority for DOL-funded job training and employment services at more than 2,400 American Job Centers, including career planning, training options and job search help.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and eligible spouses, including widows and widowers.
listings.how_to_apply: Find your nearest American Job Center at CareerOneStop.org or call 1-877-872-5627, and tell staff you are a veteran or eligible spouse.
listings.deadline: Rolling, walk in or call any time
listings.location: More than 2,400 American Job Centers nationwide
listings.source_title: Veterans | U.S. Department of Labor

listings.name: Employment Navigator and Partnership Program (ENPP)
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Veterans' Employment and Training Service
listings.summary: Free one-on-one career help for transitioning service members and their spouses at military installations, with referrals to partners offering apprenticeships, mentoring, hiring events and training.
listings.eligibility: Transitioning service members and their spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: See DOL's Employment Navigator page for participating installations; Transition Assistance Program classes are scheduled through tapevents.mil.
listings.deadline: Rolling during transition
listings.location: Military installations worldwide (37 as of Nov 2024)

capacity.served: More than 19,000 people served since the program launched in 2021

listings.source_title: US Department of Labor expands employment assistance for transitioning service members, veterans, spouses with new training, partners, service areas
listings.notes: The release did not state cost; other DOL material seen in search says services are free. DOL's VETS page says it plans in-person navigators at installations that transition more than 1,500 members a year and a virtual navigator center for others. DOL's separate Off-Base Transition Training (for veterans, Guard, Reserve and spouses) was offered in Indiana, New Jersey, New Mexico, Washington and D.C. as of that release.

listings.name: HIRE Vets Medallion Program
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Veterans' Employment and Training Service
listings.summary: DOL's yearly award for employers that recruit, hire and retain veterans. Job seekers can use the award as a sign of veteran-friendly employers.
listings.eligibility: Employers apply; veterans do not apply to this program.
listings.how_to_apply: Employers apply through HIREVets.gov. Veterans can look for the HIRE Vets Medallion when choosing employers.
listings.deadline: Not published on the page read

capacity.served: 772 employers received 2026 HIRE Vets Medallion Awards; over 2,300 employers have earned it since 2017

listings.source_title: Veterans' Employment and Training Service | U.S. Department of Labor
listings.notes: Employer recognition, not a direct veteran benefit. The DOL Nov 2026 award release itself could not be fetched; figures are from DOL's VETS page.

listings.name: Homeless Veterans' Reintegration Program (HVRP)
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Labor, Veterans' Employment and Training Service
listings.summary: DOL-funded local organizations give veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness job skills training, connections to apprenticeships or on-the-job training, and job placement help.
listings.eligibility: Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact an HVRP grantee organization in your area; DOL's HVRP page has program information. Grants go to organizations, not to individuals.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.source_title: Veterans' Employment and Training Service | U.S. Department of Labor
listings.notes: DOL's VETS page reports HVRP grants of over $37 million to 98 organizations in June 2025. No veteran participant counts were published on the page read; a grantee locator was not checked.

listings.name: Dole Caregiver Fellows
listings.summary: A multi-year leadership fellowship that trains military and veteran caregivers to build support in their communities and share their stories with national leaders.
listings.eligibility: Spouses, parents, family members and loved ones age 22+ who care for a wounded, ill, injured or aging service member or veteran, from any U.S. state or territory.
listings.how_to_apply: Watch the Fellows page for the next application cycle; questions go to the Foundation's fellows application email listed there.
listings.deadline: Applications for the 2026 Fellowship have closed; next cycle not yet announced

capacity.served: Nearly 290 Fellows in total

listings.source_title: Dole Caregiver Fellows - The Elizabeth Dole Foundation
listings.notes: Per-class size not published.

listings.name: Bob Hope Critical Financial Assistance Program for Military & Veteran Caregivers (Hope Fund)
listings.organization: Elizabeth Dole Foundation with the Bob & Dolores Hope Foundation
listings.summary: Grants for military and veteran caregivers facing urgent bills such as a utility shutoff, food insecurity or disaster damage, with resource navigation for every eligible applicant even if not funded.
listings.eligibility: Caregivers age 18+ of a wounded, ill or injured veteran or service member (including survivors who gave care in the last 12 months), with financial need, living in a U.S. state or territory; household income generally $150,000 or below.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the caregiver intake form on the Hope Fund page, then email the Foundation's resource navigation team that it is submitted (mark it urgent if it is). Have proof of the veteran's service ready.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: Bob Hope Critical Financial Assistance Program For Military & Veteran Caregivers - Hidden Heroes
listings.notes: Grant amount not published. Payments go to vendors, who must provide a W-9.

listings.name: EDF Connect Caregiver Community
listings.summary: A free, private online peer-support community for military and veteran caregivers to connect, learn and share resources; it replaced the former Hidden Heroes Facebook group.
listings.eligibility: Caregivers of veterans or service members of any era (pre- or post-9/11), verified with a DD-214, VA or DoD ID, VA benefits award letter or VA caregiver award letter.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the join form with a verification document; approval takes 2-3 business days, then you get an email invitation to create an account.
listings.deadline: Rolling, join any time
listings.source_title: Join The Community
listings.notes: The page does not mention a cost; no cost is stated anywhere on the Foundation pages read.

listings.name: Federal hiring authorities for military spouses and veterans' family members
listings.summary: Agencies can hire certain military spouses without competition, and some spouses, widows and parents of veterans can claim 10-point derived veterans' preference.
listings.eligibility: Noncompetitive hiring: spouses of active-duty members, spouses of members retired or separated with a 100% disability rating, and unremarried spouses of members killed on active duty. Derived preference: spouses of veterans who can't work in their field due to service-connected disability, unremarried widows or widowers of qualifying veterans, and some parents of deceased or disabled veterans.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply on USAJOBS with documents proving eligibility (SF-15 for derived 10-point preference). For DoD's Military Spouse Preference, contact your local DoD civilian personnel office.
listings.deadline: Rolling; each job posting has its own closing date
listings.source_title: Veteran Family Members - OPM.gov
listings.notes: Agencies use these authorities at their discretion; none guarantees a job.

listings.name: Federal veterans' preference and veteran hiring authorities
listings.summary: Eligible veterans get 5 or 10 extra points on many federal job applications, and agencies can hire some veterans without competition through the VRA, the 30% disabled veteran authority and VEOA.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with an honorable or general discharge. 5-point: qualifying active-duty periods or campaigns. 10-point: service-connected disability or Purple Heart. VRA: up to GS-11 for certain veterans, including those separated within 3 years. 30% authority: service-connected disability of 30% or more. VEOA: preference eligibles or veterans with 3+ years of honorable active service. Retirees generally qualify only if disabled or retired below major.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply to federal jobs on USAJOBS and check each announcement's 'Who May Apply.' Attach your DD-214 (member 4 copy), and for 10-point preference an SF-15 and VA disability letter.
listings.deadline: Rolling; each job posting has its own closing date
listings.source_title: Vets - OPM.gov
listings.notes: Preference does not apply to promotions, transfers or reassignments. Schedule A covers people with certain disabilities.

listings.name: Hero Miles
listings.summary: Free round-trip airline tickets, paid with donated frequent flyer miles, so families can visit a wounded, injured or ill service member in treatment, or so the service member can travel home on leave.
listings.eligibility: Wounded, injured or ill service members (including activated Guard and Reserve) in treatment at an authorized medical center, and their family or close friends, when not eligible for government-funded travel; also families attending a dignified transfer of a service member killed in an overseas post-9/11 contingency operation.
listings.how_to_apply: The service member requests tickets through a caseworker, social work staff or service casualty office; all requests must come through authorized contacts.
listings.deadline: Rolling, request any time
listings.location: Requested through military medical centers and casualty offices
listings.source_title: Hero Miles - Fisher House Foundation
listings.notes: Mainly for currently serving members in treatment, not separated veterans. Partner airlines: Alaska, Delta, Frontier, United.

listings.name: Hotels for Heroes
listings.summary: Free hotel rooms, paid with donated hotel points, when a Fisher House is full or unavailable during a significant medical event.
listings.eligibility: Mainly service members and their families. Veterans qualify only when the request comes through a Fisher House that would have housed them but is full. Hospitals without a Fisher House are approved case by case.
listings.how_to_apply: Ask the Fisher House manager or the hospital case worker/military liaison to submit the request; individuals cannot apply directly.
listings.deadline: Rolling, as needed
listings.source_title: Hotels for Heroes - Fisher House Foundation
listings.notes: Fisher House's Hero Miles airline-ticket program is limited to active-duty service members and their families, not veterans, so it is not listed separately.

listings.name: Fisher House Lodging
listings.summary: Free private suites with shared kitchens and living areas, close to the hospital, for families of veterans and service members receiving medical care at military and VA medical centers; Hotels for Heroes covers a hotel room when the house is full.
listings.eligibility: Families of veterans of all eras and service members in treatment; each hospital or installation sets its own eligibility and priorities.
listings.how_to_apply: Find the Fisher House at or near your medical center and contact its house manager, or ask the patient's case manager or social worker for a referral.
listings.deadline: Rolling, request any time
listings.location: 100+ houses at military and VA medical centers, including Ohio houses at the Dayton VA Medical Center, Wright-Patterson Medical Center, Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center and Cincinnati VA Medical Center

capacity.served: 570,000 families served; 13.4 million+ days of lodging; $690 million saved by families; 100+ houses in operation
capacity.figure_date: Cumulative as shown on the homepage, page read 2026-11-27 (no year stated)

listings.source_title: Houses - Fisher House Foundation
listings.notes: Hotels for Heroes applies only when a Fisher House would house the family but is full, or for patients at hospitals without a house (case by case).

listings.name: Scholarships for Military Children
listings.organization: Fisher House Foundation (administered by Scholarship Managers)
listings.summary: $2,000 college scholarships for children of active-duty, Guard/Reserve, retired or deceased service members. At least one award goes to each commissary location that receives qualified applications.
listings.eligibility: Unmarried dependent children under 23 with a valid Uniformed Services ID card whose parent or sponsor is active duty, Reserve/Guard, retired or deceased from the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard or Space Force. Must attend or plan to attend full time in a bachelor's program or a community college transfer program. GPA 3.0 (high school) or 2.5 (college). Full-scholarship recipients and service academy appointees are not eligible.
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online during the window: complete every form tab, write a 500-word essay (topic announced at opening), submit transcripts and validate eligibility with the benefits number on the back of the ID card.
listings.deadline: 2027-2028 application opens Dec 9, 2026 and closes Feb 10, 2027 at 9:00 p.m. Mountain
listings.source_title: Scholarships for Military Children - Fisher House Foundation
listings.notes: Applicant counts are not published. Applicants do not need to live near a commissary. The phone is Fisher House Foundation's main line.

listings.name: Folds of Honor Military Scholarships
listings.summary: Need-based scholarships for spouses and children of fallen or disabled U.S. service members. College and trade-school awards are up to $2,500 per term ($1,250 part time); K-12 awards cover private school (up to $5,000 a year) or tutoring.
listings.eligibility: Spouses and dependents of U.S. service members who were killed or disabled (a separate track covers first responders' families). The incident does not have to have happened on duty. College applicants need a 2.0 or higher term GPA for the two most recent fall and spring terms. Awards cover unmet need only; reapply each year.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Folds of Honor scholarship portal during the yearly window. Award offers go out by the end of July.
listings.deadline: Applications open Feb 1 to Mar 31 each year; the window is currently closed
listings.source_title: Scholarships – Folds of Honor
listings.notes: The scholarship page publishes no counts of awards or applicants.

listings.name: Veteran Career Readiness Program
listings.summary: A free 10-week career program with live classes, personal guidance and employer engagement, held in person in 10 cities and in virtual regional cohorts. FourBlock also runs a military spouse program.
listings.eligibility: Transitioning service members, veterans, student veterans and military spouses. Placement depends on timing and program fit.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the online application (about 3 minutes) and pick up to two preferred locations or formats.
listings.deadline: Spring and fall cohorts; dates vary by location and are not posted
listings.location: In person in Atlanta, Boston, Charlotte, Colorado, JBLM, National Capital Region, New York City, San Antonio, Seattle and Tampa, or virtual regional cohorts
listings.source_title: Program Registration
listings.notes: FourBlock says its alumni include 'thousands' of veterans and spouses but publishes no exact counts.

listings.name: Freedom Alliance Outdoor Adventures
listings.summary: Group outdoor trips such as fishing weekends, hunts and the Freedom Cruise for combat veterans, grouped by deployment and shared experience.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 service members and veterans with 1+ combat deployments who also served in a combat arms MOS and engaged the enemy (CIB, CAB, CAR, etc.), received a Purple Heart, received a valor award, or served in Special Operations with multiple combat deployments.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the online application linked from the Outdoor Adventures page; Freedom Alliance selects and groups applicants.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.travel: Trip locations vary. Cost and travel coverage not published on the page read.
listings.source_title: Outdoor Adventures - Freedom Alliance
listings.notes: Toll-free 800-475-6620. Freedom Alliance also runs War Heroes on Water, couples and caregiver retreats with the same combat criteria.

listings.name: Assistance Dogs for Veterans (Operation Freedom)
listings.summary: Free PTSD and mobility service dogs for veterans and first responders, with free training support for the life of the partnership.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, first responders and active-duty military with PTSD and/or TBI; people with mobility disabilities (mobility applications accepted only by referral from the Client Services team). No VA rating required for PTSD dogs.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the pre-application questionnaire and online application with a medical form, references and emergency contacts; an interview and household background checks follow before accepted applicants join the waitlist.
listings.deadline: Not published; mobility applications only by invitation
listings.travel: Facility and interviews in Englewood, CO; travel coverage not published

capacity.waitlist: Approximate wait to receive a service dog is currently 2 to 3 years

listings.source_title: Apply For An Assistance Dog - Freedom Service Dogs
listings.notes: Other pages of the site say inquiries are paused or limited to PTSD dogs; whether applications are open today is unclear. A year of sobriety is required before waitlisting for applicants with a substance use history.

listings.name: Custom Homebuilding (Specially Adapted Smart Homes)
listings.summary: Builds 100% mortgage-free custom smart homes with specialized adaptive features for America's most severely wounded veterans.
listings.eligibility: Severely wounded veterans (and severely injured first responders); detailed criteria are not published on the page.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the Apply here link on the Custom Homebuilding page to submit an application.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.served: 106 custom homes for severely wounded heroes nationwide

listings.source_title: Custom Homebuilding | Gary Sinise Foundation
listings.notes: Formerly described as the R.I.S.E. program; the current page does not use that name. The apply link goes to a form hosted on a third-party form service, so the program page is given as the apply URL.

listings.name: Snowball Express
listings.summary: Year-round support for children and surviving spouses of fallen heroes, including a five-day holiday retreat at Walt Disney World, three-day empowerment workshops, a Remembrance Garden and local community events.
listings.eligibility: Families (surviving spouses or guardians and children) of a fallen military or first responder hero who served on or after 9/11.
listings.how_to_apply: New families complete the preliminary registration form through the Foundation's community portal on the Snowball Express page.
listings.deadline: Rolling registration; retreat held each year around the holidays (dates not published)
listings.location: Walt Disney World Resort, Florida (retreat); local events nationwide
listings.travel: Five-day retreat at Walt Disney World Resort, Florida; whether travel is covered is not stated on the page read
listings.cost: Not stated on the page read

capacity.served: 28,537 loved ones of America's fallen heroes have joined the Foundation's retreats and community events

listings.source_title: Honoring Families Of Fallen Heroes | Gary Sinise Foundation
listings.notes: Apply URL is the program page the Snowball Express link resolves to. Documentation requirements are on the FAQ but the answer did not load.

listings.name: Give an Hour no-cost counseling for military and veterans
listings.summary: Confidential one-on-one counseling with volunteer licensed mental health professionals, plus free peer support groups, at no cost.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty military, Reserve, National Guard and veterans; spouses and caregivers in some cases.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the Connect to Support form on giveanhour.org to be matched with a provider, or join a weekly Military and Veterans peer support group.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Providers nationwide; in person, phone or video
listings.source_title: Mental Health Care for Military and Families - Give an Hour
listings.notes: Not an emergency service; in crisis call or text 988. Older Give an Hour materials say discharge status does not matter.

listings.name: Repair Corps
listings.organization: Habitat for Humanity with The Home Depot Foundation
listings.summary: Critical repairs to veterans' homes that fix health, safety and code problems, funded by The Home Depot Foundation and done by participating local Habitat offices.
listings.eligibility: Any honorably discharged veteran. The home must be owned (not rented) and a veteran must live there as the primary residence. Local Habitat selection criteria apply: need, willingness to partner and ability to repay.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact your local Habitat for Humanity office to ask whether it runs Repair Corps and how to apply.
listings.deadline: Set by each local Habitat office
listings.cost: Not published; local Habitat offices may ask for partial repayment

capacity.served: 70+ local Habitat offices in 30+ states completed Repair Corps projects on over 1,997 veteran-occupied properties

listings.source_title: Habitat for Humanity's Repair Corps program | Habitat for Humanity
listings.notes: Only select local Habitat offices take part; the page does not list which ones.

listings.name: Veterans Build
listings.summary: Through local Habitat offices, veterans can become homeowners with an affordable mortgage on a home they help build, or get critical home repairs, plus volunteer and job opportunities.
listings.eligibility: U.S. veterans, service members and their families; each local Habitat office sets its own income and selection criteria (need, willingness to partner, ability to pay).
listings.how_to_apply: Contact your local Habitat for Humanity office to find a Veterans Build program and apply to become a Habitat homeowner or for home repairs.
listings.deadline: Set by each local Habitat office
listings.location: Through local Habitat for Humanity offices nationwide
listings.cost: Affordable mortgage for homeownership; repair costs vary by local office

capacity.served: 9,097+ veterans and their families have partnered with Habitat to improve their housing since 2013; 350+ local Habitat offices take part

listings.source_title: Veterans Build | Habitat for Humanity
listings.notes: Not free housing: Habitat homeowners pay an affordable mortgage. See also the Repair Corps listing.

listings.name: The Headstrong Project trauma treatment
listings.summary: Donor-funded, confidential PTSD and trauma therapy with matched licensed clinicians, in person or by video, independent of VA and DoD. Up to 30 sessions are fully covered.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and family members; eligibility depends on where you live and your connection to military service (Headstrong materials describe post-9/11 veterans and service members regardless of discharge status).
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the Connect to Care form; a care coordinator schedules a 20-30 minute video intake and matches you with a therapist.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: In person in served states and by telehealth
listings.cost: Free for the first 30 sessions; a modest client co-pay after session 30. No insurance required.
listings.source_title: How Treatment Works - The Headstrong Project
listings.notes: State coverage varies; check eligibility page for your state. Post-9/11 wording comes from a Headstrong resource page seen in search, not the treatment page itself.

listings.name: Helmets to Hardhats
listings.organization: Helmets to Hardhats (North America's Building Trades Unions)
listings.summary: The building trades unions' veteran program connects veterans to registered construction apprenticeships, where apprentices earn a paycheck from day one and can also use GI Bill benefits.
listings.eligibility: Veterans; no prior construction experience needed. Each trade's apprenticeship sets its own entry requirements.
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account on Helmets to Hardhats' career site, search apprenticeships by trade and apply to openings.
listings.deadline: Rolling; each apprenticeship opening has its own timing
listings.source_title: Apprenticeship, Earn While You Learn – Helmets to Hardhats
listings.notes: The site says 'tens of thousands' of veterans have entered trade apprenticeships but publishes no counts.

listings.name: Heroes' Legacy Scholarship
listings.organization: Fisher House Foundation (administered by Scholarship Managers)
listings.summary: College scholarships for children of service members who died on active duty or were disabled on or after September 11, 2001.
listings.eligibility: Dependent, unmarried children under 23 with a valid uniformed services or DoD dependent ID, whose parent died on active duty on or after Sept. 11, 2001, or was disabled and qualified for TSGLI, or has a 100% permanent and total disability rating. Must attend or plan to attend full time in a bachelor's program or a community college transfer program. GPA 3.0 (high school) or 2.5 (college).
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply online during the window. Submit the sponsor's DD214 or DD1300, documents showing the death, TSGLI eligibility or disability, and transcripts; a parent or guardian signs online.
listings.deadline: 2027-2028 application opens Dec 9, 2026 and closes Feb 10, 2027 at 9:00 p.m. Mountain; recipients notified in June
listings.source_title: Heroes' Legacy Scholarship - Fisher House Foundation
listings.notes: Fisher House does not publish the number of awards; it depends on book royalties and donations. The Army benefits site lists the 2027-2028 award as $1,000 and gives slightly different dates (Dec 11, 2026 to Feb 12, 2027); Fisher House's own dates are used here. Students may apply to both this and Scholarships for Military Children.

listings.name: Heroes on the Water
listings.summary: Free kayak fishing and outdoor recreation events run by volunteer chapters, plus therapeutic programs with VA medical centers.
listings.eligibility: U.S. active-duty military, veterans, law enforcement, first responders and their families.
listings.how_to_apply: Find your local chapter on the chapters and events map and sign up for its events.
listings.deadline: Rolling; chapter events year-round
listings.location: 55 volunteer chapters in 26 states, including Ohio
listings.source_title: Heroes on the Water Supporting Veterans Through Fishing
listings.notes: Chapter count (55) and state count (26) are this researcher's count of the chapter list on the chapters page, not a published figure, so left out of capacity.

listings.name: Higher Ground week-long programs for veterans
listings.summary: Free week-long therapeutic recreation programs (skiing, ice climbing, fishing, outdoor adventure) for individual veterans and veteran couples, plus one-day local events.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and active-duty members with visible or invisible disabilities; some programs are for couples, some for individual veterans, and the Montana program is for veterans with TBI and/or polytrauma (VA or physician paperwork required).
listings.how_to_apply: Contact Higher Ground through the program listing or its contact page to request an application (info@highergroundusa.org).
listings.deadline: 2027 programs: Idaho snow sports Jan 3-8 (individuals) and Jan 24-29 (couples); NY ice climbing Feb 7-12; Arkansas couples Mar 7-12; Montana disabled veterans Apr 4-9; Texas bass fishing Apr 21-27
listings.location: Sun Valley, ID; Keene, NY; Jasper, AR; Big Sky, MT; Rising Star, TX
listings.travel: Program sites in ID, NY, AR, MT and TX. Listings say Higher Ground covers program costs; travel is stated as covered for the Texas program and not stated for the others.

capacity.slots: 8 couples or 7-10 individual veterans per week-long program (2027 listings)

listings.source_title: Veterans Program Type: Week Long Programs - Higher Ground
listings.notes: Small cohorts; apply early.

listings.name: Corporate Fellowship Program
listings.organization: Hiring Our Heroes (U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation)
listings.summary: A free 12-week SkillBridge fellowship that places transitioning service members with host companies four days a week, with weekly professional development, aimed at a job offer.
listings.eligibility: Service members on active duty or transition leave who are within 180 days of separation during the 12-week program, meet education and leadership requirements, and get command approval under DoD SkillBridge rules.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online; a program manager for your chosen location emails you with next steps. If you hear nothing in three business days, contact your area's program manager.
listings.deadline: 2027 Cohort 2 (May 3 to Jul 22, 2027): apply by Feb 11, 2027. Cohort 3 (Aug 30 to Nov 18, 2027): apply by Jun 10, 2027. Late applicants can be reviewed for off-cycle starts.

capacity.served: 1,261 fellows placed with over 300 host companies in 2020; 86% job placement rate

listings.source_title: Corporate Fellowships - Hiring Our Heroes
listings.notes: HOH publishes no current cohort size or applicant counts; the most recent figures found are from 2020-2021 (its first 2021 cohort had more than 500 service members). Veterans who have already separated are not covered by this program.

listings.name: Military Spouse Fellowship (MSCAP) and Military Spouse Career Accelerator
listings.organization: Hiring Our Heroes (U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation)
listings.summary: Fellowships that place military spouses with employers for hands-on work experience; the Military Spouse Career Accelerator is a paid 12-week fellowship.
listings.eligibility: Spouses of currently serving Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force and Space Force members, including active Reserve and National Guard.
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account on DoD's Spouse Education and Career Opportunities (MySECO) site with DS Logon, register on the MSCAP page, then finish the fellowship application from the confirmation email. Questions: MSCAP@uschamber.com.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Employers nationwide; spouse cohorts listed at Fort Carson, Fort Cavazos, JBLM, National Capital Region, San Antonio, San Diego and Tampa/Orlando
listings.cost: Free; the Career Accelerator fellowship is paid
listings.source_title: Internships - Hiring Our Heroes
listings.notes: No cohort sizes or applicant counts published.

listings.name: Skilled Trades Academy
listings.organization: Hiring Our Heroes (U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation)
listings.summary: A free six-week, in-person construction training fellowship with hands-on instruction and supplies for military-connected job seekers.
listings.eligibility: Military-connected job seekers pursuing construction careers. Hiring Our Heroes' industry programs are aimed at veterans and transitioning service members.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through Hiring Our Heroes' fellowship application and choose Skilled Trades Academy.
listings.deadline: Not published
listings.travel: Held in person in Jacksonville, N.C. (the application notes multiple locations); travel and lodging coverage not published
listings.source_title: Internships - Hiring Our Heroes
listings.notes: HOH also lists Manufacturing and Automotive Skilled Trades Academy tracks without details.

listings.name: Home Base Intensive Clinical Program
listings.summary: A two-week intensive clinical program for invisible wounds such as PTSD and TBI, plus family support, Families of the Fallen and New England outpatient and fitness programs, at no out-of-pocket cost.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and their families (Home Base has served people from all 50 states).
listings.how_to_apply: Use the 'Get Care' link on homebase.org to contact the team about treatment options.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Massachusetts (national intensive program; outpatient care in New England)
listings.travel: Massachusetts. Travel and lodging coverage for the intensive program not confirmed on the page read.

capacity.served: 65,000+ veterans, service members and family members received care since 2009

listings.source_title: Homepage | Home Base
listings.notes: Two-week length is from a description on the Home Base home page; a third-party resource list says Home Base serves veterans of all eras regardless of discharge status, not confirmed on Home Base's own page. 'Get Care' page could not be read (fetch budget ran out).

listings.name: Specially Adapted Custom Homes
listings.summary: Builds and donates mortgage-free, specially adapted custom homes for severely injured post-9/11 veterans, in the community the veteran chooses.
listings.eligibility: Severely injured in the Iraq or Afghanistan theaters after 9/11/2001; retired or in the process of retiring from service; approved for the VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant (or SHA for loss of use of both hands); passes criminal and credit background checks; will live in the home and can afford upkeep, taxes, insurance and utilities.
listings.how_to_apply: Get VA SAH eligibility first (VA Form 26-4555), then submit the online inquiry; HFOT contacts you within 7 business days and releases a full application once it receives your SAH rating narrative.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Homes built where the veteran chooses to live; headquarters in Taunton, Massachusetts
listings.cost: Free (no mortgage; 10-year lien, with equity starting in year six)

capacity.served: Homes built for over 435 veterans to date
capacity.waitlist: About 24 to 36 months from acceptance into the HFOT family to the key ceremony
capacity.figure_date: To date as of FAQ page last modified October 15, 2026

listings.source_title: Help for Injured Veterans – Homes For Our Troops
listings.notes: Veterans who have not used their full SAH grant are asked to direct the remaining balance to HFOT. Finalists attend a conference in Massachusetts before selection.

listings.name: Honor Flight (hub trips and Lone Eagle program)
listings.summary: Free one-day trips to Washington, D.C. to visit the war memorials, run by local hubs. Veterans far from a hub, or critically ill, can go through the Lone Eagle program.
listings.eligibility: Senior veterans who served up through May 1975 (pre-May 7, 1975 service); WWII and terminally ill veterans get priority, then others by application date. Lone Eagle serves eligible veterans not covered by a local hub.
listings.how_to_apply: Find the hub that covers your county on honorflight.org and apply through it. If no hub serves you, apply to Lone Eagle online (help: eagle@honorflight.org).
listings.deadline: Rolling; trips scheduled by each hub
listings.location: Trips depart from local hubs to Washington, D.C.
listings.travel: Washington, D.C. Trip is free to the veteran and paid for by donors; guardians pay their own share (Lone Eagle guardian donation $600).
listings.source_title: Lone Eagle Applications - Lone Eagle Honor Flight
listings.notes: Honorflight.org shows counters for veterans honored and national waitlist, but they rendered as 0 when read, so no figure recorded. Eligibility era and priority also from honorflight.org pages seen in search; Ohio has several hubs (find by county).

listings.name: Critical Needs Assistance
listings.summary: Direct financial help with urgent rent, mortgage or utility payments for qualified applicants, plus one-on-one case management, financial coaching and referrals.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 combat-wounded veterans and their families, veterans experiencing homelessness, and veterans who survived military sexual trauma (MST).
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the brief Connect to Services application; a HOPE team member calls to review your situation and eligibility.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.served: 48,800 military lives impacted by HOPE in 2025 (all programs); more than 203,900 served since 2006
capacity.waitlist: Support may take 3-4 weeks to process (not an emergency program)

listings.source_title: Critical Needs Assistance For Veterans & Service Members | HOPE
listings.notes: Served figures are organization-wide, not specific to Critical Needs. Funded in part by Wounded Warrior Project.

listings.name: Military Spouse and Caregiver Scholarships
listings.summary: Scholarships of $1,800 to $2,500 for post-9/11 military spouses and caregivers at accredited U.S. colleges, universities or trade schools, in five tracks from entry-level training to doctoral study, including one for spouses of the fallen.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 military spouses and caregivers. Restoring Family is for spouses of the fallen; Restoring Hope is for master's or doctoral study in social work, psychology or mental health counseling; other tracks cover associate, bachelor's and graduate study.
listings.how_to_apply: Go to hopeforthewarriors.org and choose 'connect to services' to request the application. Scholarships are awarded twice a year.
listings.deadline: Awarded twice a year; the spring 2026 cycle closed Sep 30, 2025 and the next dates are not yet posted

capacity.served: 290 scholarships totaling $737,107 since 2006

listings.source_title: Application open for spring 2026 Hope For The Warriors Military Spouse and Caregiver Scholarships - Hope for the Warriors
listings.notes: Detailed eligibility (for example any injury or disability requirement for the service member) is on the application, not the announcement page. No newer cycle announcement was found.

listings.name: Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans (EBV)
listings.organization: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, Syracuse University
listings.summary: Free startup training: about 30 days online, then a weeklong residency at a partner university, with travel and lodging covered. Versions serve military families (EBV-F), Wounded Warrior Project alumni and established businesses (EBV Accelerate).
listings.eligibility: EBV: post-9/11 veterans with an honorable discharge, or active duty within 180 days of separation, in early startup. EBV-F: spouses and family of post-9/11 veterans with service-connected disabilities or of active-duty members, and surviving spouses or adult children of those who died in service. EBV Accelerate: veteran-owned (50%+) businesses running 3+ years with 5+ full-time employees.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through IVMF's EBV page with a letter of recommendation written for EBV (not from a family member). Admissions are rolling; apply 3 to 4 months before a program.
listings.deadline: Rolling; no fixed deadline. 2027 dates not yet posted (2026 sessions ran February to October)
listings.location: Online, then a residency at a partner university (such as Syracuse, UConn, Missouri, Wright State, UCCS, Saint Joseph's, Texas A&M, UCLA or Florida State)
listings.travel: Travel, lodging and meals covered for EBV, EBV-F and EBV-WWP; EBV Accelerate covers lodging and meals but not travel
listings.source_title: Entrepreneurship Bootcamp for Veterans (EBV) | IVMF
listings.notes: IVMF says 83% of EBV graduates since 2007 remain in business; it publishes no graduate or applicant totals. Applications stay active for two years.

listings.name: Military Founders Lab
listings.organization: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, Syracuse University
listings.summary: A 10-week program with expert guidance and peer cohorts for veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs whose businesses are already operating.
listings.eligibility: Veteran and military spouse entrepreneurs with an operating business.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the Military Founders Lab link on IVMF's entrepreneurship programs page.
listings.deadline: Not published
listings.cost: Not published on the overview page
listings.source_title: Entrepreneurship | IVMF
listings.notes: Bunker Labs' website now redirects to IVMF and its Veterans in Residence program is not listed; Military Founders Lab is IVMF's current program for operating businesses. Details from IVMF's overview page only.

listings.name: Onward to Opportunity (O2O)
listings.organization: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, Syracuse University
listings.summary: Free online or on-installation career training with prep for 40+ industry certifications, an advisor, career coaching and employer connections. One certification exam is paid for transitioning members and unemployed veterans or spouses.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty members (transitioning), Selected Reserve, veterans and military spouses. Exam funding goes to those enrolling during transition from active duty and to unemployed veterans or military spouses; employed veterans and spouses can still take the training.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit IVMF's 'apply now' interest form, then complete the online assessment and orientation; enrollment staff place you in a learning pathway.
listings.deadline: No deadline published; apply through the interest form
listings.location: Online, or in person at some military installations

capacity.served: 50,000th participant began a cohort in November 2020

listings.source_title: Getting Started - D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families
listings.notes: No newer participant or graduate totals were published on the IVMF pages read. O2O does not use GI Bill benefits.

listings.name: STRIVE (Startup Training Resources to Inspire Veteran Entrepreneurship)
listings.organization: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, Syracuse University
listings.summary: Free program for veterans, service members and military spouses at the idea stage: an online orientation and six to nine weekly in-person classes at a partner community college.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and military spouses in the earliest stages of starting a business.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through IVMF's STRIVE application; contact your nearest partner school with questions.
listings.deadline: Not published
listings.location: In person at partner schools including Hillsborough Community College (FL), East Tennessee State, Pellissippi State (TN), Pima Community College (AZ), Kennesaw State (GA), Dallas College, Houston City College and Lamar University (TX), Miami Valley Entrepreneurs Center (OH), Metropolitan Community College (NE), Kaua'i Community College (HI), Central Oregon Community College, Diablo Valley College (CA) and the Utah Veteran Business Resource Center
listings.source_title: STRIVE | IVMF
listings.notes: The page says ten schools but lists fourteen. Phone is IVMF's general line. No participant counts published.

listings.name: V-WISE (Veteran Women Igniting the Spirit of Entrepreneurship)
listings.organization: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, Syracuse University
listings.summary: Entrepreneurship training for women veterans and military spouses: a four-week online course, then a three-day in-person capstone conference.
listings.eligibility: Women veterans and military spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the V-WISE link on IVMF's entrepreneurship programs page.
listings.deadline: Not published
listings.location: Online, plus a three-day in-person conference (location not listed on the overview page)
listings.cost: Not published on the overview page
listings.source_title: Entrepreneurship | IVMF
listings.notes: Details come from IVMF's entrepreneurship overview; V-WISE's own page was not read. IVMF says the program has run for over 15 years.

listings.name: Veteran EDGE
listings.organization: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, Syracuse University
listings.summary: A three-day national conference for established veteran- and military-spouse-owned businesses; the fee includes three nights of lodging and most meals.
listings.eligibility: Veteran and military spouse business owners in business at least one year with $100,000 or more in yearly revenue ($250,000+ preferred).
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through IVMF's Veteran EDGE application; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
listings.deadline: Rolling; discounted registration ends Nov 28, 2026; event Mar 10-12, 2027
listings.travel: March 10-12, 2027 in Dallas; fee covers three nights' lodging and most meals; participants pay their own travel
listings.cost: $499 advanced registration through Nov 28, 2026 (25% off the final price)
listings.source_title: Veteran EDGE | IVMF
listings.notes: The page says the event has more than 350 attendees without saying per year or in total.

listings.name: Warrior & Service Dog Program
listings.summary: Free service dog, plus on-campus housing, meals, equipment, vet care and about three weeks of residential training, for veterans with PTSD, traumatic brain injury or military sexual trauma.
listings.eligibility: Veterans of any era with a verified clinical diagnosis of PTSD, TBI and/or MST (does not need to be combat-related), living in the 50 states, Puerto Rico or Guam.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Warrior & Service Dog Program page with a physician's report, mental health verification form, support agreement naming two contacts, DD-214 (member 4 copy) and a full-length photo. A background check and phone interview follow.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Ponte Vedra, Florida (national headquarters) and the Warrior Ranch in Helotes, Texas
listings.travel: Residential training (stated as 18 days on one part of the page and three weeks elsewhere) in Ponte Vedra, FL or Helotes, TX. Housing, meals, equipment and on-campus vet care are covered; the veteran pays travel to and from training.
listings.cost: Free (veteran pays own travel to campus)

capacity.served: More than 1,000 Warriors paired with service dogs since 2011
capacity.slots: About a dozen veterans arrive for training each month

listings.source_title: Warrior & Service Dog Program - K9s For Warriors
listings.notes: The 'about a dozen a month' and 18-24 month wait figures are on the program page; the 1,000+ paired figure is on the FAQ page. The FAQ lists 800-273-8255, which is the former Veterans Crisis Line number, not a K9s line, so no phone is given here.

listings.name: Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation Scholarships
listings.summary: Need-based scholarships of $2,500, $5,000, $7,500 or $10,000 a year for children of Marines and of Navy Corpsmen, Chaplains and Religious Programs Specialists who served with Marine units, for college or career and technical education.
listings.eligibility: Child of a Marine, or of a Navy Corpsman, Chaplain or Religious Programs Specialist attached to a Marine unit. Cumulative GPA of 2.00 or higher. Family adjusted gross income at or below $134,000 (tax year 2025, for the 2027-2028 application); higher incomes are considered only in extreme circumstances.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at mcsf.org between January 1 and March 1. Career and technical education applications are accepted all year.
listings.deadline: Online application open Jan 1 to Mar 1 each year; career and technical education applications accepted year-round

capacity.served: 2,882 scholarships awarded, $11.7 million ('this year' on the foundation's 2024-25 fact sheet)

odds.text: The foundation says it funded every eligible applicant in 2024-25.

listings.source_title: Scholarship FAQs - Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation
listings.notes: MCSF's fact sheet says 100% of eligible applicants receive scholarship support and the average award is $4,070 a year. The sheet says 'this year' without naming it; its file is labeled 24-25. Award amounts are not guaranteed year to year.

listings.name: Microsoft Software & Systems Academy (MSSA)
listings.summary: Free 17-week, full-time technical training in cloud application development, server and cloud administration, or cybersecurity operations, fully funded by Microsoft, with connections to hiring partners.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and retirees, Coast Guard, National Guard and Reserve members, and U.S. or U.K. service members within six months of separation or retirement. Active-duty applicants need a separation date within 180 days of the start and command approval. You must finish the LinkedIn Learning path for your track and commit full time (8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday to Friday).
listings.how_to_apply: Submit basic information during the two-week window, send documents by the materials cutoff (10 weeks before start), then interview. Decisions come about 3 to 4 weeks before the cohort starts.
listings.deadline: Apply by Nov 30, 2026, 5:00 p.m. Pacific for the Apr 5 to Jul 30, 2027 cohorts
listings.location: Online (live instruction and virtual labs) on Pacific or Central time; MSSA-Europe on Central European Time

capacity.served: More than 3,900 graduates (the same page also states 4,500 graduates)

listings.source_title: (MSSA) Microsoft Software and Systems Academy – Microsoft Military Affairs
listings.notes: MSSA says each cohort has a set, limited number of seats and admission is competitive, but publishes no applicant counts. It reports a 94% graduation rate and 96% employment for graduates seeking work. MSSA is unpaid training, not an internship.

listings.name: Homes4WoundedHeroes (Mortgage-Free Homes)
listings.summary: Awards mortgage-free homes, with three years of family and financial mentoring, to combat-wounded veterans and unmarried Gold Star spouses.
listings.eligibility: Veterans wounded in combat or combat training in any American conflict (Purple Heart recipients get priority), honorably retired or separated or within 90 days of discharge; or unmarried Gold Star spouses of service members killed in action or in combat training. Must use the home as a primary residence and not currently have a mortgage.
listings.how_to_apply: Browse available homes on the Foundation's site, then complete the combat wounded veteran application or the Gold Star spouse application.
listings.deadline: Rolling; tied to homes available at the time
listings.location: Homes in cities listed on the Foundation's site; office in San Antonio, Texas

capacity.slots: Two available homes (Chicago and Houston) were listed when the page was read

listings.source_title: Homes4WoundedHeroes / Mortgage-Free Homes — Military Warriors Support Foundation
listings.notes: No total homes-awarded figure is published on the page read.

listings.name: Mission 22 Recovery + Resiliency and Elements
listings.summary: No-cost wellness programs for veterans and families: Recovery + Resiliency (coaching, biometrics, nutrition, fitness and mindfulness, with a 90-day R+R Coaching option) and Elements, a free 28-day virtual self-guided program.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and their families (focus on PTS, TBI and MST); Elements is open to anyone.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact Mission 22 through its contact page or info@mission22.com; enrollment steps are not published.
listings.deadline: Not published
listings.source_title: FAQs - Mission 22
listings.notes: Mission 22's free wellness supplement program page shows 'Applications Closed'. R+R Coaching page does not state eligibility or open enrollment.

listings.name: Move United Warfighters adaptive sports
listings.summary: Free adaptive sports for service members and veterans with permanent physical disabilities: 70+ sports through local member organizations and a calendar of military-specific events.
