listings.eligibility: Service members and veterans with a permanent physical disability (e.g., amputation, TBI, visual impairment, spinal cord injury, muscle, burn or nerve damage), injured pre- or post-2001, combat or non-combat.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the online Warfighters application; qualified applicants get a welcome email within about 10 business days and then program notices.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.cost: Free to the warfighter and family

capacity.served: More than 21,556 warfighters and family members served since the program began

listings.source_title: Warfighters - Move United
listings.notes: A Move United referral form states PTS alone does not qualify; a physical disability is needed.

listings.name: Interest-free Loans & Grants
listings.summary: Interest-free loans and grants for food, rent, utilities, car repairs, medical and dental bills not covered by insurance, funerals and other emergencies.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty or retired Sailors and Marines, their eligible family members with military ID, surviving spouses, and Reservists on extended active duty of 30 days or more. Veterans who did not retire are not listed.
listings.how_to_apply: Find your nearest NMCRS office on the website and schedule an appointment; services are free and confidential.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: NMCRS offices on Navy and Marine Corps installations; remote help available

capacity.served: More than $47 million in financial assistance to almost 40,600 active duty and retired Sailors, Marines and family members in 2025; over 211,000 used NMCRS programs and services

listings.source_title: Interest-free Loans & Grants | Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society
listings.notes: For military retirees, families and survivors only. NMCRS also offers emergency travel assistance and education grants.

listings.name: NMCRS Education Assistance Program
listings.summary: Need-based scholarships ($500 to $3,000) and interest-free loans for children and spouses of Sailors and Marines, for undergraduate, master's or career and technical study.
listings.eligibility: Children under 23 who are dependents of active-duty, retired or deceased Sailors or Marines; spouses of active-duty or retired Sailors or Marines (career and technical, first bachelor's, or master's); Sailors and Marines in MECEP/MECP (loans only). Students must keep a 2.0 GPA at an accredited school.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through NMCRS's education application portal during the spring window.
listings.deadline: 2026-2027 window ran Feb 16 to Apr 17, 2026; 2027-2028 dates not yet posted

capacity.served: $517,000 in scholarships and $44,000 in interest-free loans; nearly 500 families supported
capacity.figure_date: Prior year, as reported in NMCRS's Feb 2026 release

listings.source_title: Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society Opens Applications for 2026–2027 Education Assistance Program
listings.notes: The release counts families, not students, and does not say how many applied.

listings.name: Joanne Holbrook Patton Military Spouse Scholarships
listings.summary: One-time awards, averaging $500 to $5,000, toward military spouses' degrees, professional licenses, relicensing costs and some business expenses.
listings.eligibility: Spouses of post-9/11 service members in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, Coast Guard, USPHS or NOAA who are active duty, retired (including medically), 100% disabled veterans, Guard, Reserve or fallen. Must have or be eligible for a military or uniformed services ID. No GPA or full-time requirement.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through NMFA's scholarship page and upload your documents with the application. Submit a new application each scholarship year (Oct 1 to Sep 30).
listings.deadline: Rolling, open year-round; winners chosen quarterly (2027 rounds announced by the end of February, June and October 2027); scholarship year ends Sep 30

capacity.served: 662 military spouses selected, $833,675, in 2025

odds.text: 662 of 9,816 applicants were selected in 2025: about 1 in 15 (6.7%).

listings.source_title: Military Spouse Scholarship FAQs - National Military Family Association
listings.notes: NMFA's application form is hosted on a scholarship software site linked from its FAQ page.

listings.name: Mortgage-Free Homes and Home Modifications
listings.summary: Builds or provides mortgage-free homes, and modifies existing homes, for veterans with service-connected injuries or disabilities, surviving spouses and injured first responders.
listings.eligibility: Veterans of all eras with a documented service-connected injury, illness or disability and demonstrated financial need; honorable or general discharge; surviving spouses of service members. Mortgage-free homes: not in bankruptcy, no felony convictions. Modifications: owner-occupied home in your name, current on mortgage and taxes.
listings.how_to_apply: Choose Mortgage-Free Home or Home Modifications on the application page, pick veteran or surviving spouse, and complete the online application; a case manager sends status updates.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: Application Information | Operation Finally Home
listings.notes: No minimum disability rating on the current page; an older brochure required a 70%+ combat-related rating. Applying does not guarantee assistance.

listings.name: Last Mission Project
listings.summary: Case-by-case financial help for combat veterans while they enter or take part in an approved inpatient treatment program for PTSD, substance use or other trauma-related conditions.
listings.eligibility: Qualifying combat veterans (and first responders) entering or in approved inpatient treatment for PTSD, substance use or other trauma-related conditions. Veterans are not eligible for the organization's general emergency assistance, which is for active-duty members and Gold Star families.
listings.how_to_apply: Email the organization at the address on its Assistance Request page with your name, branch, a short description of the need and a phone number; cases are reviewed on eligibility, urgency and available funds.
listings.deadline: No public application window; inquiries reviewed case by case
listings.source_title: Assistance Request – Operation First Response
listings.notes: The organization also offers no-cost CCNA and CompTIA Security+ certification training to qualifying veterans (Project Specialized Training).

listings.name: Critical Financial Assistance Program
listings.summary: Short-term financial help for military families in hardship, paid toward overdue bills such as rent or mortgage, utilities, car payments, food, medical, vision and home repairs.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 service members wounded, ill or injured in the line of duty; if discharged, honorable or general (under honorable conditions) discharge and within 10 years of separation. Separate tracks cover deployed E-1 to E-6 with dependents and active-duty E-1 to E-6 (food and dependent vision only).
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account or log in at the My Operation Homefront portal and submit an application. Have your DD-214 and line-of-duty or other official injury records ready; a caseworker reviews and contacts you.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: Critical Financial Assistance - Eligibility - Operation Homefront
listings.notes: Home repair help is available to all post-9/11 wounded service members. Older third-party listings mention an application window of the 1st to 10th of each month; the official pages read today publish no window.

listings.name: Permanent Homes for Veterans
listings.summary: A donated, mortgage-free home awarded after the family completes a two-year program of financial counseling and casework while living in the home.
listings.eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans and retirees of any era, plus currently serving Guard and Reserve; no injury or deployment needed. Unremarried surviving spouses of service members killed in combat or while deployed may also apply. Selection weighs finances and ties to the home's community.
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account or log in at My Operation Homefront, view available homes and apply from your dashboard.
listings.deadline: Rolling; homes are donated, so availability varies by time and place
listings.location: Donated homes in various U.S. locations as listed in the portal
listings.travel: Families move to the home's location; moving costs, a $500 deposit and utility setup are the family's responsibility
listings.cost: Free home; family pays taxes, insurance, warranty, any HOA fees and $100 a month toward closing costs during the program

capacity.served: Over 730 veterans have entered the program and over 700 families have graduated since 2012; nearly $110 million in home equity deeded
capacity.waitlist: Applications take 10-12 weeks to process after a home closes; decision 1-4 weeks after finalist interviews

listings.source_title: Permanent Homes for Veterans - Operation Homefront
listings.notes: Phone is Operation Homefront's general office line.

listings.name: Transitional Homes for Veterans
listings.summary: Rent-free homes for 2 to 3 years for transitioning and recently separated veteran families, with financial counseling; the monthly program fee is refunded when the family completes the program.
listings.eligibility: Transitioning service members who served honorably and veteran families within 10 years of discharge; no injury or combat deployment required. Families should have a planned connection (family, job or school) to the home's area.
listings.how_to_apply: Create or log in to a My Operation Homefront account and use View Homes and Apply from your dashboard; selection takes about 90 days on average.
listings.deadline: Rolling; homes are listed as they become available
listings.location: Homes in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Texas
listings.travel: Families move to the home's location; moving costs not stated as covered
listings.cost: Rent-free; refundable monthly program fee set by the financial counselor, a non-refundable $1,000 deposit, plus utilities and routine upkeep

capacity.waitlist: About 90 days on average to select a family

listings.source_title: Transitional Homes for Veterans - Operation Homefront
listings.notes: Only the selected family is contacted. Phone is Operation Homefront's general office line.

listings.name: Transitional Housing (Villages)
listings.summary: Rent-free, fully furnished apartments with utilities and internet for 8 to 18 months, plus casework and financial counseling, for wounded, ill and injured service members and their families while they medically separate and wait for VA compensation.
listings.eligibility: Wounded, ill or injured service members with families who are about to medically separate or have recently separated and are awaiting VA disability compensation.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the My Operation Homefront portal, or email the transitional housing team for more information.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: San Diego, California; Gaithersburg, Maryland; San Antonio, Texas
listings.travel: Apartments are near military and VA medical centers in the three cities; travel costs not stated as covered
listings.source_title: Transitional Housing (Villages) - Operation Homefront
listings.notes: Families must attend support groups, workshops and benefits briefings. Phone is Operation Homefront's general office line.

listings.name: Operation Second Chance retreats
listings.summary: All-inclusive recovery retreats, from short local overnights to longer trips, for wounded veterans, couples, families, caregivers and Gold Star families, including Heroes Ridge at Raven Rock in Maryland.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with a military or VA rating of 70% or higher, or active duty with a Purple Heart; honorable discharge on DD214 required; combat-related injuries get priority.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the online support/retreats application with required documents and choose 'Retreats'; after verification you receive a detailed interest form. Applying does not guarantee a spot.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Retreats in MD, PA, MT, FL, TX, CO, SD, NY, DE, ID, OR, NM, VA, NH and IA
listings.travel: Retreat sites in 15 states. Retreats are all-inclusive at no cost; travel coverage not spelled out.
listings.source_title: RETREATS - Operation Second Chance
listings.notes: Toll-free 888-672-4838 also listed.

listings.name: Service Dog Program
listings.summary: Fully trained service dogs, with service dog and training fees waived, for veterans and service members with physical disabilities, PTSD, TBI or military sexual trauma.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and active-duty service members with mobility impairments or diagnosed PTSD, TBI, MST or other trauma-related conditions, considered case by case. Does not provide balance, hearing, medical alert, autism or emotional support dogs.
listings.how_to_apply: When the waitlist is open, submit the Assistance Dog Application with a photo, DD-214 copy, personal and professional references, a one-page letter and provider medical forms. Eligibility review takes about 8 weeks.
listings.deadline: Waitlist closed when checked on 2026-11-27; it reopens on a rolling basis
listings.location: Facilities in the Northwest, Southwest, Southeast and South Central regions; national headquarters in Canyonville, Oregon
listings.travel: Two-week Service Dog Team Training at the nearest PPH facility plus a home visit. Travel, housing and food during training are not covered.
listings.cost: Free dog and training (veteran pays travel, lodging and food during training and the dog's ongoing care)

capacity.waitlist: Waitlist closed; matching can take two years or more after selection

listings.source_title: Apply for a Service Dog | Get Your Assistance Dog Today — Paws for Purple Hearts
listings.notes: The organization recommends applying to other programs as well. Veterans can also apply separately to adopt a free 'career change' dog.

listings.name: Military Heroes Individual Grant
listings.summary: One-time grants for veterans facing extraordinary circumstances, covering personal emergencies such as home repairs, or job and community leadership costs such as training or travel to events.
listings.eligibility: Veterans facing extraordinary circumstances with costs they cannot cover on their own; discharge and era rules are not stated. Not for medical bills, personal travel, cosmetic home improvements, funeral expenses or disaster relief.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the PenFed Foundation Military Heroes grant page with proof of service (DD-214, LES or military ID), a description of the need and a bill, estimate or invoice. The Foundation aims to respond within 10 days.
listings.deadline: Rolling, first come first served while funds last

capacity.waitlist: Response within 10 days; longer in high-volume periods

listings.source_title: Military Heroes Individual Grant
listings.notes: Grant amount not published. The document checklist appears under the disaster relief questions on the same page; the page does not confirm it applies to this grant.

listings.name: Project Healing Waters Fly Fishing
listings.summary: Ongoing free fly fishing, fly casting, fly tying and rod building classes through local programs, plus one-day and multi-day fishing trips; all equipment provided.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with a VA disability rating, a referral from VA medical staff, or a military service rating while awaiting a VA rating; active-duty members wounded, ill or injured in the line of duty with a military provider's recommendation.
listings.how_to_apply: No application form: find your nearest of 183 local programs on the locations page and contact it, or email FieldSupportAdmin@ProjectHealingWaters.org.
listings.deadline: Rolling; classes are ongoing
listings.location: 183 local programs in 43 states and D.C.

capacity.served: 6,056 injured and disabled service members and veterans served in 2023

listings.source_title: FAQs : Project Healing Waters
listings.notes: Out-of-area trips usually open up after learning basics in a local program.

listings.name: Project Sanctuary therapeutic family retreats
listings.summary: Six-day therapeutic retreats for military and veteran families (lodging, meals, activities and family portraits included), followed by long-term family support.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty service members and veterans of all branches and eras, including Guard and Reserve, with their immediate family; single veterans welcome.
listings.how_to_apply: Register and complete the application at projectsanctuary.us/forms, choose a retreat, sign the family agreement, and pay the $100 refundable commitment fee.
listings.deadline: Rolling; retreat schedule posted for 2026 and 2027
listings.location: About 20 retreats a year in three states (Colorado-based organization)
listings.travel: Retreat sites in three U.S. states. Travel to and from the retreat is not provided; family support staff help families with financial need find travel resources.
listings.cost: Free retreat; $100 commitment fee refunded after completing the retreat
listings.source_title: FAQs - Project Sanctuary
listings.notes: Late cancellation forfeits the fee and requires a two-year wait. Families can attend one family retreat and one couples retreat, at least two years apart.

listings.name: Camp Hope interim housing program
listings.summary: Residential interim housing program in Houston for combat-trauma recovery, with peer mentoring, weekly sessions with licensed clinicians, VA navigation and aftercare planning.
listings.eligibility: Veterans struggling with combat trauma/PTSD (formal criteria not published); families are also served.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the Resident Application and Self Assessment on ptsdusa.org, or call the 24/7 Combat Trauma Help Line.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.travel: Houston, Texas (residential, about six to nine months). Travel coverage not published.
listings.source_title: Camp Hope - PTSD Foundation of America
listings.notes: Page says 44% of veterans have graduated from the program (undated outcome, not a count). Its '2025' stat counters (beds, intake) rendered as 0, so no capacity figure recorded. Office line 832-912-4429. Stay length about six to nine months.

listings.name: Veterans Aging in Place and Veteran Home Opportunity Program
listings.summary: Free home modifications and repairs (accessible bathrooms, ramps, wider doors, grab bars, exterior repairs) so veterans can stay safely in their homes, plus a path to homeownership for disabled veterans who don't own a home.
listings.eligibility: Veterans of all eras and branches. Age 59 or younger: at least a 10% service-connected rating; 60 or older: no rating needed. Honorable, general or other-than-honorable discharge. For repairs, must have lived in the home at least a year and own it or be current on the mortgage.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the online Application for Assistance (a family member or representative may apply for the veteran). Staff contact you within 7-10 business days and schedule a home assessment.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Online or by mail; headquarters in Statesville, North Carolina, with local chapters

capacity.waitlist: Large application backlog; applicants may wait 12-18 months before their application is reviewed

listings.source_title: Application For Assistance - Purple Heart Homes
listings.notes: The application page itself says contact within 7-10 business days; a separate program page warns of a 12-18 month backlog before review. For emergencies such as no heat or water, call after applying.

listings.name: PVA Sports and Recreation programs
listings.summary: Adaptive sports and recreation including a bass fishing tournament series, trapshooting, air guns, boccia, bowling, pickleball, paracycling, wheelchair basketball and rugby, outdoor recreation and online programs, plus co-presenting the Wheelchair Games.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with disabilities interested in adaptive sports; event-specific rules apply (eligibility not spelled out on the sports page).
listings.how_to_apply: Use 'Get Connected' on PVA's Sports & Recreation page to sign up for in-person and online events, or email pvasports@pva.org.
listings.deadline: Rolling; FY27 event schedule posted by PVA
listings.source_title: Sports & Recreation - Paralyzed Veterans of America
listings.notes: PVA benefits helpline 866-734-0857.

listings.name: Free Home Repairs and Modifications
listings.summary: Local affiliates make free repairs and safety and accessibility changes (ramps, grab bars, roofs, HVAC, windows, smoke alarms) for low-income homeowners, most often veterans, older adults and people with disabilities.
listings.eligibility: Usually low-income homeowners at or below 80% of local area median income; each local affiliate sets its own rules, and some serve veterans specifically or help renters.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the online map to find the nearest Rebuilding Together affiliate and contact it to apply.
listings.deadline: Set by each local affiliate
listings.location: More than 100 affiliates in 38 states and the District of Columbia
listings.source_title: FAQ | Rebuilding Together
listings.notes: Coverage depends on a local affiliate; Ohio affiliates exist (for example Dayton, which serves Montgomery County seniors and reports 6-12 month processing on its own page, not read in full).

listings.name: Salesforce Military
listings.summary: Free online Salesforce skills training with career paths. Finishing a required learning path earns a voucher for a Trailhead Academy class or a certification exam (about $200).
listings.eligibility: Current and transitioning service members, veterans of all eras, military spouses, and Gold Star children in the U.S. Service must be with the U.S., Canada, U.K., Australia or New Zealand.
listings.how_to_apply: Create or log in to a Trailhead account, verify military status through Military Connect, pick a career path and complete the required modules.
listings.deadline: Rolling, join any time
listings.source_title: Salesforce Military: Learn Tech Skills, Land A Dream Job
listings.notes: Instructor-led class seats are limited and may take weeks to open. No member or hiring counts published.

listings.name: Financial Assistance Program
listings.summary: One-time help with rent or mortgage, car expenses, utilities and other everyday bills for post-9/11 veterans rated 100% service-connected who are in VA treatment.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans, active duty, Reserve and Guard members with a 100% VA service-connected rating who are in a VA hospital or a mental health, rehabilitation or substance abuse program (inpatient or outpatient, confirmed by a letter); the need must be medical or military related; U.S. resident.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online with your DD-214 or statement of service, state ID, a provider or case manager letter and the monthly bill (plus lease and landlord W-9 for rent). Allow 3-4 weeks for processing.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Online or by mail; office in Palatine, Illinois

capacity.served: 28,000 veterans, service members and family members assisted; $10 million in emergency financial assistance provided since inception
capacity.figure_date: Since inception, as shown on the homepage read 2026-11-27

listings.source_title: Get Assistance – Salute, Inc.
listings.notes: One-time assistance only; screenshots of bills are not accepted.

listings.name: Save A Warrior residential program
listings.summary: Intensive small-group residential program (described as 72 hours) for complex post-traumatic stress, built on meditation practice and peer support, held on the organization's Ohio property.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty military and veterans of any era struggling with complex post-traumatic stress (combat arms or Iraq/Afghanistan service not required); also sworn Ohio police, fire and EMS. Program is alcohol- and drug-free.
listings.how_to_apply: The warrior must apply personally, on a computer (not a phone), through the application at saveawarrior.org/apply.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.travel: Hillsboro, Ohio. Cost and travel coverage not published on the pages read.

capacity.waitlist: Organization states it receives applications from far more warriors than it can serve (no number published)

listings.source_title: APPLY - Save A Warrior
listings.notes: Hillsboro location is from Save A Warrior's own documents seen in search; the apply page names only Ohio. In Ohio, so relevant to local listings too.

listings.name: Boots to Business
listings.summary: SBA's free two-day introduction to entrepreneurship, taught on military installations and off base as Boots to Business Reboot, with a free online follow-on course.
listings.eligibility: Service members including National Guard and Reserve, veterans, and military spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: On base, sign up through your installation's transition program. Off base, sign up for Boots to Business Reboot through the Boots to Business site or a Veterans Business Outreach Center. Questions: boots-to-business@sba.gov.
listings.deadline: Rolling; classes scheduled year-round
listings.location: Military installations, off-base classes and online

capacity.served: Nearly 260,000 service members, veterans, Guard and Reserve members and military spouses trained since 2013

listings.source_title: Boots to Business - Small Business Administration

listings.name: Veterans Business Outreach Centers (VBOC)
listings.summary: SBA-funded centers give free business planning, training and counseling, help finding loans and grants, and guidance on government contracting and veteran business certification.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, active-duty members, National Guard and Reserve, military spouses and eligible family members starting or growing a business.
listings.how_to_apply: Find your center at sba.gov/vboc and contact it for counseling or training.
listings.deadline: Rolling, contact any time
listings.source_title: SBA Announces $4.9M in Grant Awards to Expand VBOC Network | U.S. Small Business Administration
listings.notes: 51 locations as of Sept 2026, with new centers in Alaska, Florida and Louisiana. Clients served are not published.

listings.name: Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert)
listings.summary: SBA certifies veteran-owned (VOSB) and service-disabled veteran-owned (SDVOSB) small businesses so they can compete for set-aside and sole-source federal contracts.
listings.eligibility: Small business at least 51% owned and controlled by one or more veterans (service-disabled veterans for SDVOSB), meeting SBA size standards for a NAICS code in its SAM profile. A spouse or caregiver may help manage if a permanently and totally disabled owner can't.
listings.how_to_apply: Create an account and apply at certifications.sba.gov, which also has checklists and an eligibility check.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.served: More than 10,400 applications approved in the program's first year (Jan 2023 to Jan 2024)

listings.source_title: Veteran small business resources & certifications - Small Business Administration
listings.notes: SBA reported a 15-day average processing time in the first year. SDVOSBs compete government-wide; VOSBs mainly at VA. No applicant total published.

listings.name: Service Member & Family Support Program (Financial & Family Assistance)
listings.summary: Needs-based financial grants and lifetime case management for critically wounded, ill and injured service members, veterans and their families, covering bedside support, housing, transportation, adaptive equipment, caregiver retreats and disaster relief.
listings.eligibility: Combat wounded, critically ill and catastrophically injured service members and veterans of all branches (including Reserve) and their families; mainly post-9/11, with a separate program for Vietnam veterans catastrophically injured in combat. Each request is reviewed case by case.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the Connect with a Case Manager form on the Fund's Financial & Family Assistance page, or call the Fund. A case manager contacts you by your preferred method.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.served: Over 45,000 service members, veterans and families assisted to date; more than $330 million in support provided
capacity.applicants: An average of 170 grant requests processed per day
capacity.waitlist: Emergency requests typically delivered within 24-48 hours; non-urgent cases within a week
capacity.figure_date: To date as of the page read 2026-11-27 ($330M figure dated 2024)

listings.source_title: About Us - Semper Fi & America's Fund
listings.notes: The Fund also runs Tim & Sandy Day Canine Companions (service dogs), Team Semper Fi adaptive sports and an apprenticeship program. Formal eligibility rules are not spelled out on the pages read; the case manager screens.

listings.name: Semper Fi & America's Fund Integrative Wellness (incl. Team Semper Fi adaptive sports)
listings.summary: Recovery and wellness programs for wounded, ill and injured service members and veterans: the Team Semper Fi adaptive sports program, NeuroFitness, post-traumatic stress support, canine companions, and arts and music.
listings.eligibility: Critically wounded, ill and injured service members, veterans and military families from all branches.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the 'Connect with a Case Manager' form on thefund.org or call; a case manager follows up.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.source_title: Integrative Wellness - Semper Fi & America's Fund
listings.notes: The Fund also gives direct financial aid, adaptive equipment and home/vehicle modifications, and runs the LCpl Parsons Welcome Home Fund for Vietnam veterans with service-connected injuries or Agent Orange illnesses.

listings.name: Sentinels of Freedom Bridge for Education
listings.summary: Personal support for severely wounded post-9/11 veterans returning to school or work: education support through graduation, mentors, housing subsidies and pro bono help such as tutoring, financial planning and resume help.
listings.eligibility: Severely wounded or injured post-9/11 veterans committed to returning to school or work as their injuries allow.
listings.how_to_apply: Start from the Apply Now page or contact Sentinels of Freedom by email (contact@sentinelsoffreedom.org) or phone.
listings.deadline: Not published
listings.source_title: Sentinels of Freedom - Veterans Support Programs
listings.notes: Application criteria and steps are not spelled out online; program appears active (2026-2027 events posted).

listings.name: Stop Soldier Suicide (ROGER wellness service)
listings.summary: Free, confidential suicide-specific care by telehealth, including counseling, crisis intervention and safety planning.
listings.eligibility: All U.S. veterans and service members, plus loved ones worried about someone; no proof of service or particular discharge status required.
listings.how_to_apply: Reach out through stopsoldiersuicide.org or call for immediate confidential support.
listings.deadline: Rolling

capacity.served: 6,000+ service members and veterans served; 21,400+ requests for help (past 10 years)

listings.source_title: Stop Soldier Suicide
listings.notes: General line 844-889-5610. In crisis, dial 988 then press 1.

listings.name: Student Veterans of America Scholarships
listings.summary: SVA's partners fund about $90,000 a year in scholarships, including five $10,000 John Edelman awards for mental health counseling students and $10,000 RTX awards for Navy and Army student veterans.
listings.eligibility: Student veterans. Edelman awards: students pursuing mental health counseling. RTX SPY-6: U.S. Navy student veterans. RTX Patriot: U.S. Army student veterans (fields such as engineering, operations, logistics, manufacturing).
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the MySVA portal during the spring window; each award has its own page with requirements.
listings.deadline: 2026 window ran Mar 31 to May 1, 2026; next window not yet posted

capacity.slots: 9 scholarships in the 2026 cycle (5 Edelman, 2 RTX SPY-6, 2 RTX Patriot)

listings.source_title: Scholarships - Student Veterans of America®
listings.notes: Applicant counts are not published.

listings.name: 2027 National Military Survivor Seminar and Good Grief Camp
listings.summary: TAPS' national gathering for surviving military families, with grief seminars for adults and the Good Grief Camp for children.
listings.eligibility: Survivors grieving the death of a military or veteran loved one, and their children.
listings.how_to_apply: Watch the TAPS website for registration details, or call the 24/7 line.
listings.deadline: Event May 27-31, 2027; registration dates not published on the page read
listings.location: Not stated on the TAPS page read
listings.travel: Location and whether travel costs are covered were not stated on the page read
listings.cost: Not stated on the page read
listings.source_title: Tragedy Assistance Program For Survivors (TAPS) Is Here For You!
listings.notes: Only the dates were on the homepage; the event page itself was not read (fetch budget ran out). Confirm location and registration before publishing.

listings.name: Survivor Support
listings.summary: A 24/7 helpline, casework, peer mentors, grief counseling connections, benefits and financial assistance guidance, education support, and survivor seminars and Good Grief Camps for anyone grieving a military or veteran loved one.
listings.eligibility: Anyone grieving the death of a military or veteran loved one, regardless of relationship to the service member or the cause or circumstances of death.
listings.how_to_apply: Join online as a survivor (or connect a survivor to TAPS) on the Survivor Support page, or call the 24/7 line.
listings.deadline: Rolling, join any time
listings.location: Online, by phone and at events nationwide; headquarters in Arlington, Virginia
listings.cost: Not stated on the pages read
listings.source_title: Survivor Support | TAPS
listings.notes: Helpline is 800-959-TAPS.

listings.name: Team Rubicon disaster response volunteering (Greyshirts)
listings.summary: Veteran-led disaster relief organization where volunteers ('Greyshirts') deploy to floods, hurricanes and wildfires or serve remotely; deployment travel is paid by Team Rubicon.
listings.eligibility: Open to veterans, service members and civilians; no military requirement. Must pass a background check and complete TR101 training to deploy.
listings.how_to_apply: Sign up online, complete your Greyshirt profile in Roll Call, pass the background check and finish the TR101 course.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.cost: Free; Team Rubicon pays flights and makes travel arrangements for deployments
listings.source_title: How to Join Team Rubicon
listings.notes: Older Team Rubicon guidance also required health insurance before deploying; confirm current rules.

listings.name: Team Red, White & Blue membership and events
listings.summary: Free membership in a national veteran health and fitness community with local chapter workouts, runs, outdoor Eagle Expeditions, virtual challenges and a member app; veterans get a free performance shirt when they join.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members, military families and civilian supporters.
listings.how_to_apply: Join through the Team RWB member app (Apple or Google) or members.teamrwb.org, then RSVP to local events.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.cost: Free (some challenges offer optional paid gear packages)

capacity.served: 318,451 members and supporters at end of 2025; 14,868 in-person events in 2025

listings.source_title: Join Up - Team Red, White & Blue

listings.name: Tillman Scholars Program
listings.summary: A national scholarship and leadership program for service members, veterans and military spouses. Scholars get an award averaging $10,000 a year toward tuition, fees, books and living costs, plus leadership training and a scholar network.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty service members and veterans of all branches (including Guard and Reserve, pre- and post-9/11), and current or surviving spouses of veterans or service members. Must attend full time at an accredited U.S. college or university in a bachelor's, master's or professional program. No minimum GPA to apply; a 3.0 is needed to renew. FAFSA required.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the foundation's application page once the cycle opens. Have your essays, a 250-word biography, proof of service, one character recommendation and financial documents ready.
listings.deadline: Applications for the 2027 class open December 1, 2026; the foundation says the deadline varies by year and it is not yet posted
listings.location: Online; study at any accredited U.S. school

capacity.served: 60 Tillman Scholars selected for the 2024 class

odds.text: Fewer than 3% of applicants are chosen, the foundation says. For the 2024 class, 60 scholars were picked from nearly 1,600 applications: about 1 in 27.

listings.source_title: Pat Tillman Scholarship Application - Pat Tillman Foundation
listings.notes: The 2024 figures (60 selected from nearly 1,600 applications) are from the foundation's own June 27, 2024 press release, read as republished on Yahoo Finance, not on ptf.org. The foundation's site says only that up to 60 are chosen each year and fewer than 3% of applicants are selected. No applicant count was published for the 2026 class (announced July 9, 2026). The Dec 1, 2026 opening date is from the Army benefits site. The apply page lists two different essay formats; check the live form.

listings.name: Military Assistance Response Program
listings.summary: Short-term financial help with essential bills when a military-service-related incident causes a crisis; payments go directly to lenders, landlords, utilities and other vendors.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans, service members and their families in financial crisis because of military service or circumstances beyond their control.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the online application on the USA Cares website. A case manager calls you, a committee reviews the case, and approved applicants may need to complete financial training before funds are paid.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: How Can Veterans Apply for Help From USA Cares? - USA Cares
listings.notes: The page read is a 2022 how-to-apply article on the official site; the apply button lives on usacares.org. USA Cares also runs career transition and financial education programs.

listings.name: Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC)
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Caregiver Support Program)
listings.summary: A monthly stipend for the primary family caregiver, plus possible CHAMPVA health coverage, respite, mental health counseling, legal and financial planning, travel benefits and training, for caregivers of seriously injured veterans.
listings.eligibility: Veteran (or service member being medically discharged) with a single or combined service-connected rating of 70% or higher who needs at least six continuous months of in-person personal care. Caregiver must be 18+ and a spouse, child, parent, step or extended family member, or someone who lives with the veteran full time.
listings.how_to_apply: The veteran and each caregiver applicant (one primary, up to two secondary) complete and sign a joint VA Form 10-10CG online or by mail; a local Caregiver Support Program team member then contacts you.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Online or by mail; local VA Caregiver Support Program teams at every VA medical center
listings.source_title: Caregiver Support Program (CSP) - VA Caregiver Support Program
listings.notes: Stipend equals the GS-4 step 1 annual salary for the veteran's locality divided by 12: Level One pays 62.5%, Level Two (veteran unable to self-sustain in the community) pays 100%. Legacy participants' transition period runs through September 30, 2028. Phone is the VA Caregiver Support Line (Mon-Fri 8am-8pm ET).

listings.name: National Veterans Creative Arts Competition and Festival 2027
listings.summary: National competition in art, creative writing, dance, drama and music for veterans in VA care; gold medal winners are invited to the national festival. 2027 theme: Growth.
listings.eligibility: U.S. military veterans who are eligible for and enrolled in VA health care before submitting an entry.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit through the national submission link posted on the VA festival page during the window, or enter your local VA facility's competition (contact its recreation or creative arts therapy staff). Rules are in the 2027 Competition Handbook.
listings.deadline: National submissions Feb 1 - Mar 15, 2027; winners announced June 2027
listings.location: Entries from any VA facility; festival hosted by Orlando VA Healthcare System (2027 and 2028)
listings.source_title: National Veterans Creative Arts Festival - National Veterans Sports Programs
listings.notes: Contact VAArts4Vets@va.gov. Orlando as 2027-2028 host from an Orlando VA news release (July 2026). Festival dates not yet published; many local VA competitions closed in summer/fall 2026.

listings.name: Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA, Chapter 35)
listings.summary: Monthly education payments for spouses and children of veterans who died of a service-connected cause, are permanently and totally disabled from service, or are missing or captured. Covers degrees, vocational training, apprenticeships, on-the-job training and more, for up to 36 months (45 if training started before Aug 1, 2018).
listings.eligibility: Child or spouse of a veteran or service member who is permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected disability, died from a service-connected disability or in the line of duty, is missing in action or was captured or detained over 90 days, or is hospitalized for a permanent and total disability and likely to be discharged for it. Time limits depend on when you became eligible; none if on or after Aug 1, 2023.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at VA.gov or mail VA Form 22-5490 to VA Claims Intake Center, PO Box 5215, Janesville, WI 53547, then tell your school's certifying official. Free help is available from accredited VSO representatives.
listings.deadline: Rolling; time limits depend on when you became eligible
listings.source_title: Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Children must give up DIC payments to use DEA; spouses can receive both. You can't use DEA and the Fry Scholarship at the same time.

listings.name: Marine Gunnery Sergeant John David Fry Scholarship (Fry Scholarship)
listings.summary: Up to 36 months of Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits (tuition and fees, housing, books and supplies) for children and surviving spouses of service members who died in the line of duty on or after September 11, 2001.
listings.eligibility: Child or surviving spouse of a service member or Selected Reserve member who died on or after Sept. 11, 2001: in the line of duty on active duty, from a service-connected disability within 120 days of leaving active duty, or in the line of duty or from a service-connected disability as a Selected Reserve member. Children must be 18 or have finished high school or a GED.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at VA.gov or mail VA Form 22-5490 to VA Claims Intake Center, PO Box 5215, Janesville, WI 53547, then tell your school's certifying official. If you qualify for both Fry and DEA, you must choose one.
listings.deadline: Rolling; time limits depend on the date and circumstances of death
listings.source_title: Fry Scholarship | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Phone is VA's GI Bill line (7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Central, Monday to Friday).

listings.name: Program of General Caregiver Support Services (PGCSS)
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Caregiver Support Program)
listings.summary: Free peer mentoring, skills training, one-on-one coaching, telephone and online support, and referrals for anyone caring for a veteran enrolled in VA health care, with no rating requirement.
listings.eligibility: Caregivers providing personal care to a veteran enrolled in VA health care who needs help with daily living or supervision; the caregiver does not need to be related to or live with the veteran.
listings.how_to_apply: No formal application: contact the Caregiver Support Coordinator at the veteran's VA facility, or ask the veteran's provider for a referral, and complete an intake.
listings.deadline: Rolling, enroll any time
listings.location: Through every VA medical center; phone and online
listings.source_title: Program of General Caregiver Support Services (PGCSS) - VA Caregiver Support Program
listings.notes: Respite care is offered separately through VA Geriatrics and Extended Care. Phone is the VA Caregiver Support Line.

listings.name: GI Bill education benefits (Post-9/11 and Montgomery GI Bill)
listings.summary: VA education benefits that help pay for college, training and other approved programs. One application covers the Post-9/11 GI Bill, Montgomery GI Bill (Active Duty and Selected Reserve) and transferred benefits.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and Selected Reserve members with qualifying service, and family members using transferred Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits. Service requirements differ by program.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at VA.gov, or mail VA Form 22-1990 to VA Claims Intake Center, PO Box 5215, Janesville, WI 53547. Family members using transferred benefits use VA Form 22-1990e. Accredited VSO representatives can help for free.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: How To Apply For The GI Bill And Related Benefits | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Service requirements for each GI Bill program are on VA's separate eligibility pages, which were not read for this listing.

listings.name: National Veterans Golden Age Games 2027
listings.summary: Multi-sport competition for veterans 55 and older, with 20 medaled events, eight age groups and ambulatory, visually impaired and wheelchair divisions. The 2027 Games are in Cleveland, Ohio.
listings.eligibility: U.S. military veterans who are 55 or older by Dec 31, 2027 and enrolled in VA health care.
listings.how_to_apply: Register through the VA Golden Age Games page when registration opens and sign up there for email updates. Not enrolled in VA health care? Apply first at va.gov/healthbenefits/apply (VA Form 10-10EZ).
listings.deadline: Games June 23-29, 2027; registration dates to be announced
listings.travel: Cleveland, Ohio. Travel coverage not published.

capacity.slots: 20 medaled sports events, 8 age categories, 3 divisions (2027)

listings.source_title: National Veterans Golden Age Games - National Veterans Sports Programs
listings.notes: Contact email GoldenAgeGames@va.gov; phone is VA's general line. A July 2026 Wilmington VA news release said 2027 registration was 'now closed', but VA's official event page says registration dates are TBA; trust the official page. Hosted in Ohio in 2027.

listings.name: Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA) Grant
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Veterans Health Administration, Prosthetic & Sensory Aids Service)
listings.summary: A lifetime grant of up to $6,800 (or $2,000) for medically necessary changes to your home, such as roll-in showers, lowered counters, permanent ramps, accessible entrances and electrical or plumbing upgrades for medical equipment.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members with a medical need: $6,800 for a service-connected disability, a disability treated as service-connected, or any disability if you have a single service-connected rating of 50% or more; $2,000 for other disabilities. Renters need the owner's notarized permission.
listings.how_to_apply: Get a prescription from a VA physician describing the project and medical need, then submit VA Form 10-0103 with an itemized estimate and a color photo of the area to your local VA Prosthetics (PSAS) office.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Through your VA medical center's Prosthetic & Sensory Aids Service
listings.source_title: Prosthetic & Sensory Aids Service (PSAS) - Rehabilitation and Prosthetic Services
listings.notes: Does not cover new construction, decks, spas, security systems, removable items like portable ramps or stair glides, or routine maintenance like roofs and furnaces.

listings.name: VA Monthly Training Allowance for Paralympic and Olympic Athletes
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, National Veterans Sports Programs
listings.summary: A monthly allowance, paid at the VR&E Chapter 31 rate, for veterans with disabilities who train and compete in Paralympic sports (or Olympic sports with a 30%+ service-connected rating).
listings.eligibility: Veterans under 38 U.S.C. 101 not barred under 38 CFR 3.12. Paralympic: classified as eligible by the sport federation and meeting VA's performance standard. Olympic: 30% or higher service-connected rating and selected for a national team. Must keep training plans and submit monthly and quarterly reports.
listings.how_to_apply: Gather your VA Benefits Summary Letter, meet the published performance standard for your sport, and submit VA Form 10091 through the FSC Customer Engagement Portal. Questions: stipends4vets@va.gov.
listings.deadline: Rolling; funding limited by annual appropriations
listings.source_title: Monthly Training Allowance - National Veterans Sports Programs
listings.notes: Priority goes to veterans with service-connected disabilities. Phone is VA's general line.

listings.name: MOVE! Weight Management Program
listings.summary: VA lifestyle program that helps veterans manage weight through nutrition, physical activity and behavior change, alongside VA weight-management medicines or surgery when appropriate.
listings.eligibility: Offered through VA health care; ask your VA health care team whether you qualify (criteria not listed on the page read).
listings.how_to_apply: Use the 'MOVE! Get Started' link on move.va.gov and talk with your VA health care team.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.cost: Not published on the page read
listings.source_title: MOVE! Weight Management Program

listings.name: Service Dog Veterinary Health Benefit
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (Prosthetic & Sensory Aids Service)
listings.summary: VA pays for veterinary insurance (premiums, copays, deductibles), prescriptions and required equipment like harnesses for a guide or service dog, and covers travel to get the dog, for eligible veterans. VA does not provide the dog.
listings.eligibility: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who are prescribed a guide or service dog for a visual, hearing or substantial mobility impairment, including mobility limits caused mainly by a mental health condition. The dog must come from an Assistance Dogs International or International Guide Dog Federation accredited program.
listings.how_to_apply: Ask your VA clinical provider (or VA mental health provider for mental-health-related mobility) for an evaluation; if a dog is the right tool, the provider requests the benefit through your VA medical center's Prosthetic & Sensory Aids Service.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: VA Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service (PSAS) - Service Dog Veterinary Health Benefit - Rehabilitation and Prosthetic Services
listings.notes: Covers one dog at a time. Not covered: food, grooming, boarding, over-the-counter medicine, non-sedated dental cleaning, license tags.

listings.name: Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) and Special Home Adaptation (SHA) Grants
listings.summary: Federal grants to buy, build or change a home for veterans with certain severe service-connected disabilities: up to $133,042 (SAH) or $26,654 (SHA) for fiscal year 2027, plus a smaller grant to adapt a family member's home you are living in temporarily.
listings.eligibility: SAH: you own or will own the home and have a qualifying service-connected disability such as ALS, loss or loss of use of more than one limb, blindness in both eyes, certain severe burns, or loss of use of one leg after 9/11 that prevents walking without aids. SHA: you or a family member own the home and you have loss or loss of use of both hands, certain severe burns, or certain breathing injuries.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online, by mail or in person with VA Form 26-4555. The grant can be used up to six separate times over your lifetime.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time

capacity.slots: Only 120 veterans and service members per fiscal year can qualify on the basis of loss of one extremity after September 11, 2001 (set by Congress); no cap stated for other qualifying conditions

listings.source_title: Disability Housing Grants For Veterans | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA): up to $53,585 if SAH-eligible or $9,568 if SHA-eligible (FY 2027). The phone listed is VA's main benefits line; the page itself lists no number. SAH approval is also the entry ticket for Homes For Our Troops and some Building Homes for Heroes builds.

listings.name: Edith Nourse Rogers STEM Scholarship
listings.summary: Up to 9 extra months of Post-9/11 GI Bill or Fry benefits (or $30,000, whichever comes first) for students finishing a STEM degree, a healthcare clinical training program or a STEM teaching certification.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and Fry Scholars using Post-9/11 GI Bill or Fry benefits with 6 months or less of benefits left, who are in an undergraduate STEM program needing at least 120 semester hours with 60 completed, or who hold a STEM degree and are in a covered clinical training or teaching certification program. Priority goes first to those at the 100% benefit level.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at VA.gov (about 15 minutes). VA usually decides within 30 days; awards are made monthly and must be used within 6 months.
listings.deadline: Rolling; awards made monthly
listings.source_title: Edith Nourse Rogers STEM Scholarship | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Meeting the requirements doesn't guarantee an award. VA publishes no recipient counts on the page.

listings.name: National Veterans Summer Sports Clinic 2027
listings.summary: Five-day adaptive sports and recreation clinic with team building, arts, fitness and education for veterans in mental health care. Airfare, hotel, local transport and most meals are provided.
listings.eligibility: Veterans 55 or younger (those turning 56 in 2027 accepted), enrolled in VA care and actively seen by a VA or community mental health provider for PTSD, depression or related conditions, referred by that provider, able to travel independently, and committed to being substance-free.
listings.how_to_apply: Your mental health provider submits a referral through VA's secure referral link; after approval you complete registration and medical forms. Accepted veterans get travel details Feb 1.
listings.deadline: Registration Nov 16, 2026 through mid-January 2027, or until 150 completed registrations; clinic May 19-23, 2027
listings.travel: Orlando, Florida. Airfare, hotel, Orlando transportation and most meals provided.
listings.source_title: National Veterans Summer Sports Clinic - National Veterans Sports Programs
listings.notes: Contact summersportsclinic@va.gov. Registration closes once 150 completed registrations are received, so apply early.

listings.name: VET TEC 2.0 (High-Tech Program)
listings.summary: VA pays for non-degree high-tech training, usually certificate programs, in computer programming, software, data processing, information science and media application.
listings.eligibility: Veterans discharged other than dishonorably, or active-duty members within 180 days of separating, who served at least 36 months on active duty and are under 62 when approved.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at VA.gov.
listings.deadline: Rolling while openings remain in the fiscal year

capacity.slots: Up to 4,000 paid participants per fiscal year; 2,022 openings shown as of Nov 10, 2026

odds.text: Capped at 4,000 paid participants a year; VA showed 2,022 openings left on Nov 10, 2026.

listings.source_title: VET TEC 2.0 (high-Tech Program) | Veterans Affairs

listings.name: Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E, Chapter 31)
listings.summary: Job training, education, counseling, resume help and self-employment support for veterans with service-connected disabilities, in five tracks from returning to a former job to independent living.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with a VA service-connected disability rating of at least 10% and no dishonorable discharge (a 12-year window applies if discharged before Jan 1, 2013; no limit after). Service members with a 20%+ memorandum rating, awaiting discharge for a serious illness or injury, or in IDES or the PEB process may also apply.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online at VA.gov, mail VA Form 28-1900 to VR&E Intake Center, PO Box 5210, Janesville, WI 53547-5210, or apply at a VA regional office. A counselor then decides entitlement.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31) | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: VA publishes no participant counts on the page.

listings.name: National Veterans Wheelchair Games 2027
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and Paralyzed Veterans of America
listings.summary: The largest annual wheelchair sports rehabilitation event for veterans, with many competitive adaptive sports. The 2027 Games are in Orlando, Florida.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with spinal cord injury, amputation, multiple sclerosis or another central neurological condition; the physical disability must be permanent, measurable and affect mobility. Must be eligible for care at a VA medical facility.
listings.how_to_apply: Registration is not open yet. Watch wheelchairgames.org/registration (medical criteria and clearance forms are posted there) or email NVWGInfo@va.gov; your VA recreation therapist or PVA chapter can help.
listings.deadline: Games July 14-19, 2027; registration dates to be announced
listings.travel: Orlando, Florida. Travel and lodging coverage not published on the pages read.
listings.source_title: Registration - Wheelchairgames

listings.name: VA Whole Health
listings.summary: VA wellness approach offering health and wellness coaching, well-being programs, and complementary therapies such as yoga, tai chi, meditation, acupuncture and massage, plus free Whole Health courses taught by VA staff and veteran peers.
listings.eligibility: Veterans in VA health care; availability varies by local VA facility, so check with your VA health care team.
listings.how_to_apply: Talk with your VA health care team, fill out the Brief Personal Health Inventory, and find your facility's Whole Health contact on va.gov/wholehealth.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Local VA facilities and online resources
listings.cost: Not published on the page read
listings.source_title: Whole Health Home - VA

listings.name: National Disabled Veterans Winter Sports Clinic 2027
listings.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and DAV (Disabled American Veterans)
listings.summary: A week of adaptive skiing, snowboarding and other winter sports rehabilitation in the Colorado Rockies for disabled veterans. All accepted veterans must ski.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, orthopedic amputation, visual impairment, or stroke with residual effects. PTSD, chronic pain, low back pain and arthritis alone do not qualify. Weight limits: 220 lb sit-down, 300 lb stand-up skiing.
listings.how_to_apply: Download the 2027 participant application from wintersportsclinic.org/participate and submit it complete and signed. Disabilities are reviewed by the clinic's medical and program directors.
listings.deadline: Application window opened Aug 1, 2026; clinic March 27 - April 3, 2027. Closing date not shown on the pages read (the 2026 clinic's deadline was Nov 30, 2025).

listings.source_title: Participate - National Disabled Veterans Winter Sports Clinic

listings.name: Yellow Ribbon Program
listings.summary: Helps cover tuition and fees above the Post-9/11 GI Bill cap at participating private or foreign schools, or out-of-state public schools. The school contributes an amount and VA matches it.
listings.eligibility: Must qualify for the Post-9/11 GI Bill at the 100% level (for example, 36 months of active duty with an honorable discharge, a Purple Heart after 9/11, or a service-connected disability discharge after 30 continuous days), be on active duty with 36 months of service, use transferred benefits as a spouse or child, or be a Fry Scholar. The school must take part and still have open Yellow Ribbon spots.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply for the Post-9/11 GI Bill, find participating schools with VA's Yellow Ribbon school search or the GI Bill Comparison Tool, and work with the school's certifying official.
listings.deadline: Rolling; each school caps its number of Yellow Ribbon students
listings.source_title: Yellow Ribbon Program | Veterans Affairs
listings.notes: Each school sets a maximum number of Yellow Ribbon students in its VA agreement; VA publishes no totals on the page.

listings.name: Vet Tix (Veteran Tickets Foundation)
listings.summary: Free tickets to sporting events, concerts, performing arts and family events across the country. Members pay only a small delivery fee per ticket request.
listings.eligibility: Currently serving military of all branches, honorably discharged veterans, and immediate family of troops killed in action. Service is verified at sign-up.
listings.how_to_apply: Create a free account at vettix.org and complete service verification. Then request tickets to listed events near you.
listings.deadline: Rolling, sign up any time; events are posted continuously
listings.cost: Free tickets; small delivery fee per request (amount not published on the home page)

listings.source_title: Vet Tix - Veteran Tickets Foundation
listings.notes: Hero's Wish (once-in-a-lifetime event experience) is a separate Vet Tix program for deployed troops, severely wounded warriors and KIA families.

listings.name: Veterans Airlift Command free flights
listings.summary: Free private flights on volunteer-owned aircraft for combat-injured veterans and their families, mainly for medical care, and for compassionate trips and healing events such as unit reunions.
listings.eligibility: Combat-injured veterans; family members and close friends visiting service members or veterans at medical facilities.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit a request through the Request Flight page on veteransairlift.org.
listings.deadline: Rolling; request as early as possible
listings.source_title: Home - Veterans Airlift Command | Serving Combat Veterans

listings.name: Veterans Yoga Project free classes
listings.summary: Free daily live online yoga and Mindful Resilience classes, a recorded practice library, and local classes at VA centers and community sites.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members, military families and the wider community.
listings.how_to_apply: Join a live class in the online VYP Studio or Practice Library, or find a local class on veteransyogaproject.org.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.location: Online, plus local classes at VA and community centers

capacity.served: 42,164 Mindful Resilience yoga classes taught (cumulative); 150 military community members trained as teachers

listings.notes: Site also offers Mindful Resilience teacher training for veterans.

listings.name: Veterati Mentoring
listings.summary: An online platform where veterans, service members and military spouses book one-on-one mentoring phone calls with volunteer professionals.
listings.eligibility: Transitioning veterans, service members and military spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: Sign up as a mentee on Veterati's site (about 60 seconds) and book calls with as many mentors as you like.
listings.deadline: Rolling, join any time
listings.source_title: Veterati
listings.notes: The home page read does not state the cost; 'free' comes from Veterati's own mentee sign-up and partner pages seen in search. No mentor or call counts published.

listings.name: VETRN MBA Program
listings.summary: Free online MBA-style training for established veteran-owned small businesses, with a mentor, a peer group and a written growth or turnaround plan.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service-disabled veterans, National Guard members and family members who own a small business running at least one year with a sustainable revenue model and at least $125,000 in yearly revenue, and who can commit to regular coaching.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply at vetrn.org/apply.

listings.name: VIT Academy
listings.summary: Tech training in cybersecurity, web development, data science, cloud computing, AI/ML and project management for veterans, active-duty members and military spouses, with career placement support.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, active-duty military and military spouses.
listings.how_to_apply: Register on VetsinTech's site and sign up for a class from its upcoming classes list.
listings.deadline: Not published; classes listed on VetsinTech's upcoming classes page
listings.cost: Little to no cost, per VetsinTech

listings.name: Financial Assistance for Service Members (VFW Unmet Needs)
listings.summary: A grant, not a loan, of up to $2,500 toward daily necessities such as housing, utilities and car payments, paid directly to the creditor.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty service members, including activated Guard and Reserve, and their families facing unexpected financial hardship from deployment or other military-related activity or injury.
listings.how_to_apply: Review the eligibility criteria on the VFW Financial Grants page and use the Apply Today link to the online application portal.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.source_title: Financial Grants - VFW
listings.notes: As read today the VFW page names only active-duty members and their families, not separated veterans; older VFW releases described veterans as eligible. The page body says up to $2,500 while its meta description says $1,500. Separated veterans should check local VFW posts and state departments for relief funds.

listings.name: Sport Clips Help A Hero Scholarship
listings.organization: VFW (Veterans of Foreign Wars), funded by Sport Clips Haircuts
listings.summary: Scholarships of up to $5,000 per semester toward tuition and fees for veterans and service members ranked E-5 and below, paid straight to the school.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members of any branch at E-5 or below who have finished basic training and AIT, have been accepted to a school and show financial need (a current FAFSA Student Aid Report is required; those denied federal aid aren't eligible). Active, Guard or Reserve members without a DD214 need a commanding officer's statement of service.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online once per semester through the application link VFW points to at SportClips.com/Hero. Apprenticeship or certification programs that don't follow semesters should email HelpAHero@vfw.org.

listings.source_title: VFW Sport Clips Help A Hero Scholarship Frequently Asked Questions
