listings.name: Warrior Expeditions (Warrior Hike, Warrior Bike, Warrior Paddle)
listings.summary: Long-distance outdoor therapy expeditions: the Appalachian Trail on foot, a cross-country bike route, or the Mississippi River by paddle. Gear, clothing and supplies are provided at no cost, with lodging, food and transport help from supporters along the route.
listings.eligibility: Any honorably discharged veteran who served in a combat zone.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through warriorexpeditions.org/apply before the deadline; selections are announced in January.
listings.deadline: 2027 season applications close Dec 1, 2026; selections announced Jan 7, 2027
listings.location: Appalachian Trail (GA-ME, Mar-Sep); Great American Trail (DC-WA, May-Aug); Mississippi River (MN-LA, Jun-Sep)
listings.travel: Routes span many states. Equipment and supplies provided; transportation, lodging and food are coordinated through community supporters along the route.
listings.source_title: Apply - Warrior Expeditions
listings.notes: Deadline is days away as of 2026-11-27. Contact info@warriorhike.org.

listings.name: Family and Caregiver Support
listings.summary: Free support for family members and caregivers of post-9/11 warriors: help navigating VA caregiver benefits, caregiver relief and respite through the Independence Program, mental wellness services, financial counseling, benefits help, peer connection and family events.
listings.eligibility: Family members, close supporters and caregivers of an eligible post-9/11 veteran or service member (up to three per warrior); you do not need to be related or live with the warrior, but the warrior must consider you a close support person.
listings.how_to_apply: Register online as family support on WWP's registration page (the warrior need not be registered first, but WWP verifies the warrior's eligibility), or call the WWP Resource Center.
listings.deadline: Rolling, register any time
listings.location: Online, by phone and at events nationwide
listings.source_title: Support for Veteran Families & Caregivers | WWP
listings.notes: WWP has no dedicated children's programs, but children can attend many family events. WWP does not run an emergency grant fund; for immediate needs the Resource Center refers to other help.

listings.name: Independence Program
listings.summary: Free, long-term, individualized support for catastrophically injured post-9/11 veterans: case management, goal setting, home health care, wellness and alternative therapies, long-term care planning, and caregiver respite and support.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans or service members registered with WWP who have a moderate to severe brain injury, spinal cord injury or neurological condition that makes daily living difficult (the diagnosis need not be service-related). A caregiver is not required.
listings.how_to_apply: Register with WWP online (free; verification through ID.me, Login.gov or service documents), then contact the WWP Resource Center; a family member or advocate can call on the warrior's behalf.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Nationwide, at home, independently or in assisted care
listings.source_title: Veteran Independent Living Program | Wounded Warrior Project
listings.notes: WWP registration is open to veterans who served on or after 9/11 and meet WWP's eligibility rules; a visible or combat injury is not required. Manual verification takes 5-7 business days. Other WWP programs open to registered warriors: Warrior Care Network (PTSD treatment), Project Odyssey, Financial Readiness counseling, Benefits Services and Warriors to Work.

listings.name: Project Odyssey and WWP Talk
listings.summary: Project Odyssey is a 12-week mental health workshop using adventure-based learning to build resilience; WWP Talk offers weekly one-on-one emotional support calls with a dedicated partner.
listings.eligibility: Warriors and family members registered with Wounded Warrior Project (WWP serves veterans and service members injured on or after 9/11).
listings.how_to_apply: Register with WWP online, then contact the Resource Center for a screening that matches you to programs; expect a call and email within 3-5 business days.
listings.deadline: Rolling
listings.source_title: Wounded Warrior Project - Mental Wellness
listings.notes: The mental wellness page does not itself state the post-9/11 rule; that comes from WWP's Warrior Care Network page. General line 877-832-6997.

listings.name: Warrior Care Network two-week intensive treatment
listings.organization: Wounded Warrior Project with Emory Healthcare, Mass General, Rush and UCLA Health
listings.summary: A two-week accelerated outpatient brain-health program (50+ hours) at an academic medical center for PTSD, TBI, MST and related conditions. Treatment, travel, meals and related costs are covered.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members who served on or after Sept 11, 2001, with PTSD symptoms, MST, TBI or related conditions (diagnosis not required), able to attend for two weeks, not in crisis, and able to stay substance-free during the program.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact the WWP Resource Center by phone, email (resourcecenter@woundedwarriorproject.org) or live chat; registering with WWP is free.
listings.deadline: Rolling; cohort-based
listings.location: Atlanta (Emory), Boston (Mass General), Chicago (Rush), Los Angeles (UCLA)
listings.travel: Attend at one of four academic medical centers. WWP covers treatment, travel, meals and related expenses.
listings.cost: Free, no co-pays (insurance may be billed if you have it)

capacity.served: More than 5,000 warriors have completed the program since 2015

listings.source_title: Treatment for Veterans Conditions: PTSD, TBI, and MST | WWP
listings.notes: Resource Center also 904-405-1213.

listings.name: Our Military Kids activity grants (Deployed National Guard and Reserve Program and Combat Injured Program)
listings.summary: Grants of up to $300 per child, per grant, for a child's sports, fine or performing arts, camps, tutoring, driver's education, STEM or similar activity, paid by check to the activity provider. For children of deployed Guard and Reserve members and of service members and veterans in treatment for post-9/11 combat-related injuries or illness.
listings.eligibility: Children ages 1 to 18 (or not yet high school graduates). Deployed Program: a parent or guardian in the National Guard or Reserve who is deploying or activated on a stateside mission for 60 days or more; one grant per child for 60 to 179 days within 12 months, two grants for 180 days or more; AGR, ADOS, PCS, MANDAYS, training and in-state activations over two years do not qualify, and the activity must start before the service member returns home. Combat Injured Program: a parent or guardian of any branch who is a service member on medical orders or a veteran actively receiving treatment for post-9/11 combat-related injuries or illness; veterans need an individual VA rating of 30% or more in burns, amputation, mental health, spinal cord injury, TBI, PTSD or a PACT Act presumptive condition; one grant every six months up to four per child, plus one FLEX grant. Child care, school or academic tuition and religious mission trips are not eligible.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online from the Apply page, one application per child and per activity. Deployed families send orders showing 60 or more days and proof the child is a dependent; Combat Injured families send a treatment letter from a case manager or provider (template supplied) and, for veterans, a DD214 and VA ratings by category. Include proof of the activity cost from the provider.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time; for the Deployed Program the activity must start before the service member returns home
listings.location: Online; activities anywhere in the U.S. (office in Oakton, VA)

capacity.served: 107,000 grants and $38 million awarded in total (the page does not say over what period)
capacity.figure_date: Cumulative total shown on the Impact page on 2026-11-27

listings.source_title: Apply - Our Military Kids
listings.notes: Approvals depend on available funds; the page says the organization has never turned away an eligible child. Checks are made out to the activity provider, never to family members; a family that already paid can ask for reimbursement after approval. A second ad (library id 2437471066780872, Dayton, with CareSource Military and Veterans) points to the same program.

listings.name: RecruitMilitary Career Fairs (in-person and virtual)
listings.summary: In-person and virtual hiring events where transitioning service members, Guard and Reserve members, veterans and military spouses meet employers who recruit military talent, plus an online job board. In-person fairs are held on military bases and in cities; virtual fairs are online, screen-to-screen events.
listings.eligibility: Transitioning service members, Guard and Reserve members, veterans and military spouses; the audience can vary by event (base events draw mostly transitioning service members).
listings.how_to_apply: Find an event in the RecruitMilitary event schedule, choose it and click Register; the company advises registering early to prepare.
listings.deadline: Events run through the year. The event list read on November 27, 2026 showed no upcoming Ohio, Pennsylvania or Michigan dates, so check the event schedule for the next fair near you.
listings.location: Military bases and cities nationwide, and online
listings.cost: No job-seeker fee is published on the pages read; employers pay to exhibit
listings.source_title: Career Fairs - RecruitMilitary
listings.notes: RecruitMilitary is a for-profit recruiting company paid by employers. The ads call the events free for veterans, but none of the official pages read states the job-seeker cost. The event list page returned only two October 2026 events (Fort Gordon on October 7 and a Western Region virtual fair on October 27), both past, so the live schedule may not have loaded fully. The company says it has run hiring events since 2006. Other ads for this lead: library ids 1091519570481893 and 4580141265595158.

listings.name: Gold Star Family Home Program
listings.summary: Mortgage-free homes for surviving Gold Star spouses raising young children after a service member died in service after September 11, 2001.
listings.eligibility: The surviving parent of a child of a service member who died after 9/11, either killed in action in a combat zone or during authorized training, leaving at least one biological or legally adopted child 18 or younger, or from a department-verified, service-connected toxic exposure such as burn pits, leaving at least one child 21 or younger. The couple must not have been divorced at the time of death, and the surviving parent must not be remarried, engaged or cohabitating. Priority goes to families whose immediate household is unchanged since the death.
listings.how_to_apply: Check the requirements and submit the inquiry form on the Requirements and Eligibility page.
listings.deadline: Rolling; no deadline published
listings.location: Nationwide; foundation office in Staten Island, NY
listings.source_title: REQUIREMENTS & ELIGIBILITY - Tunnel to Towers Foundation
listings.notes: Found on the foundation's site while verifying the homelessness lead. The program page says mortgage-free homes but does not say whether it pays off an existing mortgage. No count of families served is published. The phone is the foundation's main line.

listings.name: Homeless Veteran Program (National Case Management Network and Veterans Villages)
listings.summary: Case managers help veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness with temporary hotel stays, move-in costs (first month's rent, security deposit, broker and application fees), rental or mortgage arrears, utility deposits or arrears, food, child care supplies, transportation and supportive services. The foundation also runs Veterans Villages, housing with on-site services in several cities.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and their families with an honorable discharge or a discharge under conditions other than dishonorable, at least 180 days of service, and proof of homelessness or of being at risk of homelessness. The foundation may make exceptions case by case.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the inquiry form on the National Case Management Network page (new and returning applicants have separate links) and upload ID, proof of veteran status and discharge, and proof of the housing crisis. For a Veterans Village, use the Veterans Village application form. Questions go to ncmn@t2t.org; screening calls can take a few weeks.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time
listings.location: Case management in nearly every state; open Veterans Villages in Houston TX, Atlanta GA, Memphis TN, Southfield MI, North Charleston SC and Harrisburg PA, with more under construction or planned (including Cleveland, OH)

capacity.served: More than 17,500 veterans and their families provided housing assistance and supportive services (no date given)

listings.source_title: National Case Management Network - Tunnel to Towers Foundation
listings.notes: For an immediate housing crisis (eviction date, foreclosure, utility shut-off, fleeing domestic violence) the page says to email ncmn@t2t.org and also call the VA National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838. Village locations read on the Veterans Villages page; that page states no eligibility rules beyond serving homeless veterans. The phone is the foundation's main line. The ad for this lead was a sponsored segment run by Fox News, not by the foundation.

listings.name: Smart Home Program
listings.summary: Mortgage-free, accessible smart homes for catastrophically injured veterans and first responders, with features such as automated doors and lighting, wider hallways and doorways, roll-in showers, adjustable cabinets and counters, backup generators and whole-home control from a phone or tablet.
listings.eligibility: Current or former U.S. service members (and first responders) who served on or after September 11, 2001 and have a permanent, service-connected injury that significantly limits mobility and independent living, and who need home modifications where adaptive and smart home features would meaningfully improve safety and independence.
listings.how_to_apply: Review the requirements and submit the inquiry form on the Program Eligibility Requirements page.
listings.deadline: Rolling; no deadline published
listings.location: Homes built nationwide; foundation office in Staten Island, NY
listings.source_title: Program Eligibility Requirements - Tunnel to Towers Foundation
listings.notes: Home features read on the About Smart Home Program page. The pages read do not list specific qualifying injury types or how many homes have been delivered. The phone is the foundation's main line.

listings.name: Bass Military Scholars Program
listings.summary: An award of $30,000 a year toward living expenses for military veterans in on-campus graduate and professional degree programs at Vanderbilt University, on top of GI Bill and Yellow Ribbon benefits. Scholars take part in two leadership or mentorship activities each semester.
listings.eligibility: Veterans honorably discharged from the U.S. military or Coast Guard who reached grade E-4 or above and have applied to or been admitted to an eligible on-campus program: J.D. (Law School), M.D. (School of Medicine), listed M.S.N. specialties and the Master of Nursing (School of Nursing, full-time local program in middle Tennessee), M.B.A. except the Executive MBA (Owen Graduate School of Management), and listed master's programs at Peabody College. Applicants not yet discharged must be honorably discharged before the end of fall semester of their first year. Online programs are not eligible.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the program's application page between August 1 and February 15. The scholarship application is separate from admission to the degree program, which has its own requirements and deadlines. Selection is based on military record, academic history, a personal video statement and potential to positively impact society.
listings.deadline: Applications open August 1 and close February 15 each year; for summer or fall 2027 entry the window is August 1, 2026 to February 15, 2027. Scholars are notified by April 1.
listings.location: Vanderbilt University, Nashville, Tennessee (on-campus programs only)
listings.travel: Study on campus in Nashville, TN. The pages read do not mention relocation or travel costs; the $30,000 a year goes toward living expenses.

capacity.slots: Approximately 10 to 15 scholars selected each year

listings.source_title: Bass Military Scholars | Vanderbilt University
listings.notes: Program launched in 2018. Eligible degree list read on the Degree Programs page and the 10 to 15 figure on the FAQ page. The FAQ does not address renewal, spouses or currently serving Guard and Reserve members. The phone is Vanderbilt's general number; the program's own contact is the email bassmilitaryscholars@vanderbilt.edu.

listings.name: We Defy Athlete Scholarship (Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu)
listings.summary: A 12-month scholarship for disabled combat veterans who are new to Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu to train at a We Defy Approved Training Facility, with two gis and, with board approval, private coaching or special training equipment. The program is built around community, health and service.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who served in an area of combat operations, are separated or retired from active duty (current or former Guard and Reserve may apply if they meet the other criteria), have a mental or physical disability rating of 80% or higher, have an honorable discharge, and are new to jiu-jitsu (generally less than one year of training). Must commit to training at least twice a week for one year at an approved facility. A special criteria waiver may be considered case by case, for example for a training accident or sexual assault related to military service.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online on the athlete application page when the window opens, with your DD214, VA rating letter and a 60-second video on what you hope to gain. Applications are processed in the order received; approval can take up to 60 days after all materials arrive.
listings.deadline: Applications closed; the next window opens December 6, 2026 at 2 PM Eastern and often fills within hours
listings.location: We Defy Approved Training Facilities (the foundation publishes a facility map); foundation office in McKinney, TX

capacity.served: More than 2,300 scholarships awarded and more than 500 veterans currently enrolled (the page does not say over what period)
capacity.figure_date: Shown on the home page on 2026-11-27

listings.source_title: ATHLETE APPLICATION - We Defy Foundation
listings.notes: Funding is limited and the number of scholarships per window is not published. Training must be at an approved facility, so a veteran needs one within reach; the facility map was not checked. The landing page and the application page word the prior-training limit slightly differently (the application page allows a white belt with under one year of jiu-jitsu or MMA).

listings.name: Built for More
listings.summary: A free peer program for post-9/11 combat veterans that opens and closes with five-day outdoor experiences in Montana (fly fishing, hunting or photography track), with about three hours a month of online group sessions in between. Air travel, lodging, meals, instruction and gear are covered.
listings.eligibility: Post-9/11 combat veterans, shown by combat awards or service in a location where Imminent Danger Pay was received (DD214 blocks 13 and 18 or other documents; active-duty applicants may use other official combat documentation). A Purple Heart is not required. Discharge, disability rating and age rules are not published. Priority goes to veterans who feel stuck or isolated and want to rebuild purpose, resilience and a support network, and who enjoy the outdoors.
listings.how_to_apply: Applications open in cycles. Join the waitlist through the form on the Built for More page and Warriors & Quiet Waters will notify you when the next application cycle opens.
listings.deadline: Not published; applications open in cycles and cohorts launch throughout the year
listings.location: Quiet Waters Ranch and Southwest Montana (office in Bozeman, MT); hunts mostly launch from Montana
listings.travel: Five-day Initial Experience and five-day Capstone Experience in Montana, with an online phase in between. The organization covers air travel to Montana, lodging, meals, professional instruction and gear; participants generally keep the clothing and equipment issued.
listings.source_title: Built for More: Veteran Fly Fishing & Wellness Program | WQW
listings.notes: The page gives the program length inconsistently (online phase 6 to 8 months in one place, 6 to 12 months in another; the home page calls it a nine-month program). The fly fishing track is listed as powered by Wounded Warrior Project. Some fishing cohorts have gone to the Everglades and North Dakota. No participant counts are published. Service dogs allowed; the ranch accommodates many wounds and conditions.

listings.name: Military Caregivers program
listings.summary: A free five-day fly-fishing and nature retreat in Montana that gives caregivers of post-9/11 combat veterans respite and time with other caregivers. Air travel, lodging, meals, guided instruction and fishing gear, which participants keep, are covered.
listings.eligibility: The designated primary provider of personal care for a post-9/11 combat veteran, named as the Primary Family Caregiver on the joint application for the VA Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC).
listings.how_to_apply: Applications are closed for now. Enter your email on the program page to join the waitlist and be told when applications reopen.
listings.deadline: Applications closed as of November 27, 2026; next session dates not published
listings.location: Quiet Waters Ranch near Bozeman, Montana, and Southwest Montana trout streams
listings.travel: Participants fly into Bozeman, MT. The organization covers air travel to Montana, lodging, meals, professional instruction and fishing gear.
listings.source_title: MILITARY CAREGIVERS: Warriors & Quiet Waters
listings.notes: Found on the same organization's site while verifying the Built for More lead. The page does not say whether a spouse who is not the PCAFC primary caregiver qualifies. Zero alcohol and substance policy; service dogs allowed; adaptive equipment available. The page's newsletter form showed a configuration error, so the waitlist form may not work.

listings.name: National Wreaths Across America Day
listings.summary: Volunteers help lay remembrance wreaths on veterans' graves at ceremonies at more than 5,500 participating locations in all 50 states, at sea and abroad. Veterans and families can sign up to help at a participating cemetery near them.
listings.eligibility: Open to volunteers; the site lists no requirements or fee to volunteer.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the Location and Group Search on the Wreaths Across America site to find a participating location or sponsorship group near you and register to volunteer there.
listings.deadline: National Wreaths Across America Day is Saturday, December 19, 2026

listings.name: Hiring Our Heroes Small Business Grant
listings.organization: Hiring Our Heroes, U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation (supported by the FedEx Founders Fund)
listings.summary: One-time cash grants for small businesses owned by veterans and military spouses: four grants of $10,000 and one grand prize of $25,000 in the 2027 program. Winners are announced at a Hiring Our Heroes event in spring 2027.
listings.eligibility: The applicant must own 51% or more of a U.S.-based, for-profit business and be an honorably discharged veteran (active duty, Guard or Reserve), a current Guard or Reserve member, or a current military spouse, and legally live in the 48 contiguous states, Alaska or Hawaii. The business must have 3 to 20 workers (counting owners, full- and part-time staff and 1099 contractors) and under $5 million in annual revenue, and be in a zip code with a Distressed Communities Index score of 40 or higher or show financial need from hardship beyond the owner's control. Nonprofits, government entities, large franchises (over 25 corporate-owned or 50 total stores), gas stations, direct sellers, and businesses mainly in cannabis, gambling, tobacco or e-cigarettes, firearms, diet aids, religious instruction or adult content are excluded. Years in business are not stated.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Apply Now form on the Hiring Our Heroes Small Business Grant page; only online entries count. The form has eligibility questions, business details and five short essays (about 250 words each). Winners must later provide proof of service, business photos and a headshot.
listings.deadline: Applications for the 2027 program are due by 11:59 p.m. EDT, December 15, 2026. Winners are notified by March 29, 2027.
listings.location: Online; winners announced at a Hiring Our Heroes event in spring 2027 (place not published)
listings.award: Up to $25,000: four grants of $10,000 and one grand prize of $25,000

capacity.slots: 5 grants per cycle (four $10,000 and one $25,000), chosen from up to 20 semifinalists

listings.source_title: Small Business Grant Program Rules - Hiring Our Heroes
listings.notes: Also read the program page (https://www.hiringourheroes.org/small-business-award) and the application page. The rules do not mention equity; the awards are described as one-time cash grants. Applicants agree to attend the award ceremony if chosen as a finalist or recipient; travel coverage is not published. The application form's last essay still refers to a $10,000 grant. The graphic's claims (up to $25,000, 3 to 20 workers, closes Dec 15) match the official rules; the official rules add a $5 million revenue cap, a for-profit requirement, and a distressed-community or hardship requirement.

listings.eligibility: Any startup founded and actively managed by a U.S. military veteran or a veteran spouse. The official page does not state revenue, industry, location, business-age or nonprofit rules. In 2026 the finalists competed in four tracks: defense technology; energy and clean technology; health care and biotechnology; and software and information technology.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the Apply Today link on the Veterans Business Battle page at Rice Business. Finalists are invited to pitch in person in Houston.
listings.deadline: Applications to compete for the 2027 competition are open now; the application deadline is not published. The competition is March 31 to April 1, 2027. (For the 2026 event, applications closed January 31, 2026.)

listings.name: Farmer Veteran Fellowship Fund
listings.summary: Small grants of $1,000 to $5,000 for veterans in their first years of farming or ranching. The money is paid directly to approved vendors for an item the veteran needs for the farm business, such as fencing, breeding livestock, tractor implements or beekeeping equipment.
listings.eligibility: Farmer Veteran Coalition members who served or are serving in any U.S. military branch, any era; honorable discharge (other characterizations considered case by case); currently serving members need a support letter from their commander. Must have an agricultural business in operation and a business plan (nonprofits submit a strategic plan). The official pages conflict on nonprofits: the program page says for-profit only, while the FAQ says nonprofits may apply but for-profit farms get priority. No location, years-farming or disability requirement is stated. Prior recipients: the program page allows reapplying only if the earlier award was $1,000 or less; the FAQ says former recipients cannot reapply.
listings.how_to_apply: Join the Farmer Veteran Coalition, then apply online when the yearly application opens (it stays open at least four weeks). The form has short-answer and essay questions plus uploads of a business plan of up to five pages and proof of service; an advisory panel reviews applications.
listings.deadline: The 2026 cycle is complete (awardees announced May 1, 2026). The application opens once a year for at least four weeks; review is in March and awards come in spring. Next cycle dates are not announced.
listings.cost: Free to apply (no fee stated); Farmer Veteran Coalition membership required
listings.award: $1,000 to $5,000, paid to vendors for one farm item (not paid to the veteran)

capacity.served: More than 930 veterans funded and nearly $4 million awarded since 2011

listings.source_title: Farmer Veteran Fellowship Fund (Farmer Veteran Coalition)
listings.notes: Also read the Fellowship Fund FAQ (https://farmvetco.org/fvfellowship/faq/) and the 2026 awardees page. Recipients have six months to use the award, must get vendor approval first, and must send progress reports and mentor other farmer veterans. Only one item is funded per award. Equipment through Kubota's Geared To Give program uses the same application. FVC's membership page showed a 'please wait while your request is being verified' screen and was not read; that membership is free is reported only in search excerpts. The graphic's claims ($1,000 to $5,000, paid to vendors) match the official page.

listings.name: DAV Patriots Pitch
listings.organization: DAV (Disabled American Veterans), DAV Patriot Boot Camp
listings.summary: A Shark Tank-style pitch contest where veteran and military-spouse entrepreneurs selected from each DAV Patriot Boot Camp cohort pitch a panel of veteran investors and experts for non-dilutive funding. The boot camp itself is a free three-day in-person program with training, mentoring and networking.
listings.eligibility: Pitch contestants are selected from each DAV Patriot Boot Camp cohort; there is no open application for the pitch itself. The boot camp is for veterans, military-connected community members and spouses who own or founded a for-profit business that is scalable and looking to grow; franchisees and nonprofits are not eligible. An EIN, a website, and revenue or capital raised in the past year are preferred but not required. No service-connected disability requirement is stated.
listings.how_to_apply: Register for a DAV Patriot Boot Camp cohort through the Apply Now button on the Patriot Boot Camp page; seats are first come, first served, subject to eligibility. Entrepreneurs from each cohort are then selected to compete in DAV Patriots Pitch.
listings.deadline: Invite only from boot camp cohorts. Registration for the Winter 2027 DAV Patriot Boot Camp is listed with an Apply Now button, but dates, place and deadline are not yet published. Recent pitch events were in July 2026 (DAV National Convention) and October 2026 (Alumni Accelerator).
listings.location: DAV National Headquarters near Cincinnati or other U.S. cities (varies by cohort)
listings.travel: In-person three-day boot camps at DAV National Headquarters near Cincinnati or other cities. DAV covers programming, meals and event transportation for those staying at partner hotels, plus a ride back to the airport and parking; participants pay their own travel to the host city, lodging and incidentals.
listings.cost: Free (participants pay their own travel and lodging)
listings.award: Thousands of dollars in non-dilutive funding; exact amounts are not published on the official pages
listings.unconfirmed: A $10,000 prize was reported in local news about one 2026 alumni event; DAV's own pages say only thousands of dollars.

listings.name: Military Spouse Scholarship for spouse-owned businesses
listings.summary: NMFA's military spouse scholarship can also be used for a military spouse-owned business. Funding can cover business needs including inventory and merchandise, business marketing, branding, manufacturing, supplies and permits.
listings.eligibility: The spouse of a service member who served after 9/11/2001 and is active duty, retired (including medically retired), a 100% disabled veteran, Guard, Reserve, or a fallen service member, in any of the 8 Uniformed Services (Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, Space Force, Coast Guard, USPHS Commissioned Corps, NOAA). The spouse must have, or be eligible to hold, a valid military or Uniformed Services ID. The business must be military spouse-owned. Veterans themselves cannot apply, and spouses of veterans who are neither retired nor rated 100% disabled do not qualify. NMFA volunteers, employees and board members are not eligible. The page sets no revenue, employee or business-age limits and does not address nonprofits.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through NMFA's spouse scholarship site, which says applications are open. Submit a new application each scholarship year (October 1 to September 30). There is no limit on how many times you can apply and receive funding.
listings.deadline: Rolling, open year-round; a new application is needed each scholarship year (Oct 1 to Sep 30). Winners are announced in three rounds, by the last day of February, June and October 2027.
listings.award: One-time award, averaging $500 to $5,000 per the FAQ; the scholarship home page says $500 to $1,000 on average. Paid by check to the program or vendor address you give, or in some cases as a reimbursement with receipts.

capacity.served: 662 military spouses selected for a scholarship in 2025, totaling $833,675 (all scholarship uses, not business only)
capacity.applicants: 9,816 applicants in 2025 (all scholarship uses, not business only)
